A wrong parameter type or any field of the wrong type inside the receipt or a hop — including a `bool` posing as an `int` — raises `TypeError`; an empty target, an empty hop sequence or a negative moment raises `ValueError`; an illegal base receipt raises `InvalidBatchReceiptError`; an illegal delegation encoding, key set, version value or chain binding raises `InvalidReceiptDelegationError` with the first failing hop in the message; and unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a signature mismatch raise `AuthenticationError`. On success it returns a fresh mapping with the fixed keys `hops` (the hop payloads in chain order), `receipt` (the base receipt payload), `receiptDigest` (the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the base receipt bytes), `target` and `version` (the integer 1); repeated calls return equal but mutually independent results.

`verify_batch_receipt_chains(items, policy, keyring, moment)` verifies a whole batch of those delegation chains entirely offline and adds the cross-chain delegation-fork entry point, reading and writing no file and modifying no input. `items` is a non-empty list; each item contains exactly a non-empty, batch-unique `id`, the `receipt` bytes, a non-empty `hops` list of hop bytes and a non-empty `target` str, and reports strictly preserve input order. The whole batch structure is validated together with the shared `policy`, `keyring` and `moment` — which keep their single-chain validation and classification — before any chain is processed: container, element or field type faults raise `TypeError` and an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, a wrong item key set or an empty hops list raises `ValueError`; only such a batch-level fault raises. Each item then runs independently through the exact `verify_batch_receipt_chain` rules, so one chain's failure never stops a later chain or changes an earlier report: a base-receipt fault is `invalid-receipt`, a delegation encoding, key-set, version-value or chain-binding fault is `invalid-delegation` and unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a signature mismatch are `unauthenticated`, each with the non-empty exception text and a null `result`. Successful chains are grouped by `receiptDigest` and only delegation paths under the same base receipt are ever compared; within one group, the same `upstream` digest pointing at two or more distinct legitimate next-hop audiences is a fork, while a plain prefix extension of one path is not. Every chain whose path crosses a forking edge is reclassified `conflicted`, keeping its verified single-chain result with `error` fixed to `forked-delegation`. The top-level result is a fresh dict with the fixed keys `forks`, `items` and `version` (integer 1); `forks` is sorted stably by `receiptDigest` then `upstream`, each entry carrying exactly `receiptDigest`, `upstream`, ascending `audiences` and the ascending `ids` of the chains crossing that edge, and each item report carries exactly `error`, `id`, `result` (a fresh independent copy of the single-chain result when verified) and `status`. Repeated calls return equal but mutually independent results.

`sign_receipt_fork_proof(items, policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` packages that fork summary into an offline-transferable signed evidence object, reading and writing no file and modifying no input. The `items`, `policy`, `keyring` and `moment` are exactly those of `verify_batch_receipt_chains`, which runs first; a proof is issued only when the resulting summary reports at least one fork (a fork-free summary raises `ValueError`). The proof is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing newline or any other trailing byte, carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`. The payload binds exactly `issuer`, `keyVersion`, `moment`, `policy` (the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical compact policy encoding), the complete `report` and `chains`, and `version` (integer 1). `chains` summarizes every input chain strictly in input order with no reordering or omission: each entry carries exactly `id`, `digest` (the SHA-256 of that chain's base receipt bytes), `target` and `hops` (the SHA-256 of each hop's complete bytes in chain order). `signature` is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the key bound to the exact issuer and version with no fallback; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials raise `AuthenticationError`. A parameter or public field type fault raises `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int); an empty issuer, a non-positive version, a negative moment or an illegal shared policy value raises `ValueError`.

`verify_receipt_fork_proof(proof, policy, keyring, moment)` verifies such evidence entirely offline from just the proof, the expected policy, the current keyring and the verification moment — no file is read or written and no argument is modified. It recomputes the policy digest, validates the proof encoding, key sets, version, digests, recursive key ordering, the chain-material order and references, the complete bound chain-batch report (item count and per-position ids, result receipt digest/target/hop count, hop upstream chaining, and the forking edges and crossing chains recomputed from the bound results), rejects a signing moment later than the verification moment, and checks the HMAC against the key the *current* keyring binds to the payload's exact issuer and version, usable at the verification moment, so later revocation or expiry rejects the proof with no fallback. On success it returns a brand-new mapping with the fixed keys `chains`, `issuer`, `keyVersion`, `moment`, `policyDigest`, `proofDigest` (the SHA-256 of the proof bytes), `report` and `version` (integer 1). A non-bytes proof or a wrong public field type raises `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int); an illegal policy, keyring or moment raises `ValueError`; an illegal proof encoding, key set, version, digest, ordering, reference or report binding raises `InvalidReceiptForkProofError` (a `ValueError` subclass); unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a signature mismatch raise `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_receipt_fork_proofs(items, policy, keyring, moment)` verifies a whole batch of those proofs offline, never reading or writing a file or modifying an input. `items` is a non-empty list; each item contains exactly a non-empty, batch-unique `id` and the `proof` bytes. The batch and the shared `policy`, `keyring` and `moment` — which keep their single-proof validation and exception classification (a non-negative non-bool int) — are all validated before any proof is processed: container, element or field type faults raise `TypeError` and an empty list, an empty or duplicate id or a wrong item key set raises `ValueError`; only such a batch-level fault raises. Each proof is then verified independently through the exact `verify_receipt_fork_proof` rules, in strict input order, each selecting its key by its own exact issuer and version with no fallback: one proof's failure never stops a later proof or alters an earlier report, and a currently unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credential or a mismatched signature makes that item `unauthenticated`, an illegal encoding, key set, version, digest, ordering, reference or report binding makes it `invalid-proof`, and a passing proof is `verified`. The top-level result is a fresh dict with the fixed keys `items` and `version` (integer 1); each item report carries, in this key order, `error` (null exactly when verified), `id`, `result` (a fresh independent copy of the single-proof result when verified, otherwise null — the identity of an unauthenticated payload never enters a result) and `status`, each failure keeping a definite, non-empty copy of the original exception text. Repeated calls return equal but mutually independent results.

## Multi-site fork disposition decisions

`decide_forks(items, policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` turns those signed fork proofs into one multi-site disposition decision entirely offline, reading and writing no file and modifying no input. `items` is a non-empty list; each item contains exactly a non-empty, batch-unique `id` and non-empty `proof` bytes. `policy` contains exactly `action` (`"isolate"` or `"rollback"`), `base` (the existing `{"batch","sites","threshold"}` proof policy), `sites` (a non-empty map of each authorized non-empty site to its non-empty set of allowed positive key versions) and `threshold` (a positive integer no greater than the site count). Every proof is first verified through the existing receipt fork proof rules, then authorized by the exact signing site and key version with no fallback, then authenticated against the current keyring. An invalid, unauthorized or unauthenticated proof rejects only that item with one fixed reason (`invalid-proof`, `unauthorized-site`, `unauthorized-version`, `credential-unavailable`, `revoked`, `not-yet-valid`, `expired`, `bad-signature`) and never affects a later item; an identical proof digest counts once per site and extra copies are `duplicate`, while different valid proofs from the same site are a `contradiction`. The valid proofs of distinct sites must agree on every fork boundary made of the base receipt digest, the forking upstream and the target domain. A unique boundary set attested by at least the threshold of distinct sites is `accepted`, a contradiction or boundary disagreement is `conflicted`, and everything else is `insufficient`. An accepted decision recommends the policy action — isolate the deduplicated, ascending target domains, or roll back to before the fork — while every other outcome recommends `manual-review` and claims no boundary or target. The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object (recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved, no trailing byte) carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds exactly `action`, `boundaries`, `decisions` (sorted by site then id), `issuer`, `keyVersion`, `policyDigest` (the SHA-256 of the canonical policy), `proofs` (each proof digest in the original input order), `recommendation`, `targets` and `version` (integer 1), and the signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the key bound to the exact issuer and version with no fallback. Unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired signing credentials raise `AuthenticationError`; a type fault (including a `bool` posing as an int) raises `TypeError`; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id or an illegal policy value raises `ValueError`.

`verify_fork_decision(decision, policy, keyring, moment)` re-checks such a decision entirely offline from just the decision packet, the expected policy, the current keyring and the verification moment — no file is read or written and no argument is modified. It validates the canonical encoding and key sets, recomputes the policy digest and the action binding, re-tallies the bound per-proof decisions (row ordering, the original-order proof digest bindings, duplicates, contradictions, cross-site boundary agreement, the threshold and the claimed boundaries, targets and recommendation) purely from the signed payload, and verifies the HMAC against the key the current keyring binds to the payload's exact issuer and version usable at the verification moment, so a later revocation or expiry rejects it. On success it returns a fresh dict keyed `action`, `boundaries`, `decisions`, `issuer`, `keyVersion`, `policyDigest`, `proofDigest` (the SHA-256 of the decision bytes), `proofs`, `recommendation`, `status`, `targets` and `version` (integer 1). An illegal encoding, key set, digest, ordering, reference or binding raises `InvalidForkDecisionError` (a `ValueError` subclass); unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature raise `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_fork_decisions(items, policy, keyring, moment)` verifies a non-empty batch of those decisions offline and independently, in strict input order. Each item contains exactly a non-empty, batch-unique `id` and the `decision` bytes; the batch and the shared policy, keyring and moment are validated in full before any decision is verified, so only a batch-level fault raises (container/field faults `TypeError`; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id or a wrong item key set `ValueError`). Each decision is then reported in input order as `verified`, `invalid` or `unauthenticated` with the fixed key order `error`, `id`, `result` and `status`; a failed item keeps a definite, non-empty copy of the original exception text and a null result, and the identity of an unauthenticated payload never enters a result. Repeated calls return equal but mutually independent results. The existing proof interfaces and module commands are unchanged.

## Multi-site fork execution plans and confirmations

`plan_fork_execution(decision, policy, keyring, generated_at, expires_at)` turns one sealed, accepted fork disposition into a site execution plan entirely offline, reading and writing no file and modifying no input. The `decision` bytes are re-verified through the exact `verify_fork_decision` rules against the current keyring at the generation moment, and only an `accepted` decision can be planned — a `conflicted` or `insufficient` decision raises `ValueError`. The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte, carrying exactly `action`, `boundaries`, `decisionDigest`, `expiresAt`, `generatedAt`, `operations`, `policyDigest` and `version` (integer 1): it binds the decision and policy digests, the action, the inclusive validity window, every fork boundary and the deduplicated, ascending target domains — exactly one idempotent operation per target — and never copies an un-adopted proof (there is no `proofs`, `decisions` or signer field). Each operation carries exactly `action`, its target's `boundaries` (sorted), `operationId`, `requires` and `target`; the idempotent `operationId` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 over the decision digest, the action, the target domain and the canonical bytes of every related boundary. An `isolate` operation's precondition is exactly `{"state": "active"}` — the target domain must still be active — while a `rollback` operation binds `{"base", "upstream"}`, the base receipt digest and the forking upstream of its first boundary. Parameter, container or field type faults raise `TypeError` (a `bool` never poses as an int); a negative moment, a window with `generatedAt` after `expiresAt` or a non-accepted decision raises `ValueError`; an illegal decision packet raises `InvalidForkDecisionError`; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired decision credentials or a wrong signature raise `AuthenticationError`.

`confirm_fork_execution(plan, decision, policy, receipts, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` aggregates the per-site execution receipts into one signed multi-site confirmation, again entirely offline. It validates the plan packet, requires its `decisionDigest` to equal the SHA-256 of the offered decision bytes and its `policyDigest` to match the canonical policy, re-verifies the original decision against the current keyring (it must still be `accepted`) and checks that the plan regenerates byte-for-byte from the decision, the policy and its own window; the aggregation moment must not precede `generatedAt` but may lag past `expiresAt` after an outage. `receipts` is a non-empty list of canonical receipt envelopes kept in their collection order. Each receipt is one `{payload, signature}` packet whose payload binds exactly `planDigest`, `operationId`, `site`, `keyVersion`, `siteVersion`, `executionMoment`, `previous`, `result` and, for a success, `postDigest`; `result` is one of `executed`, `rejected` or `failed`, and only an executed receipt binds a post-state digest. The receipt site must equal the operation target and the key is selected by exact site and version with no fallback, required usable both at the execution moment and at the aggregation moment. A receipt for a replaced verdict, an unknown operation (or a site/target mismatch), an execution moment outside the plan window, a `previous` digest unequal to the SHA-256 of the operation precondition or an out-of-order same-site receipt rejects only that item with one fixed reason (`decision-replaced`, `unknown-operation`, `outside-validity`, `previous-mismatch`, `out-of-order`); credentials unknown, revoked or time-invalid at either moment, or a wrong signature, reject only that item as `bad-signature`; a structurally illegal receipt only records `invalid-receipt`. Identical receipt bytes count once and extra copies are marked `duplicate`; different valid results for one operation, or different executed post-state digests, are a `contradiction`. The precedence is contradiction → explicit site rejection → missing/failed operation → full success, yielding the overall statuses `conflicted`, `rejected`, `partial` and `confirmed` (a contradiction fails that operation regardless of other receipts). The result is one canonical compact `{payload, signature}` object with no trailing byte; the payload binds exactly `aggregatedAt`, `issuer`, `keyVersion`, the complete `plan`, the receipt digests in their original order (`receipts`), the per-item reason records (`reasons`, each carrying `digest`, `operationId`, `postDigest`, `result`, `reason` and `site`), the per-operation conclusions (`results`, in plan order with `operationId`, `result`, `target`), the overall `status` and `version`; the signature is the HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical payload bytes under the exact aggregator issuer/version key, following the same canonical encoding rules as the plan. Parameter/container/field type faults raise `TypeError` (a `bool` never poses as an int); an empty/null value or an illegal moment raises `ValueError`; plan/packet encoding, digest, ordering or binding faults raise `InvalidForkExecutionError` (a `ValueError` subclass), and unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired aggregator credentials raise `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_fork_confirmation(confirmation, decision, policy, keyring, moment)` re-checks one confirmation entirely offline from just the packet, the original decision bytes, the policy, the current keyring and the verification moment — no file is read or written and no argument is modified. It validates the canonical encoding and key sets, regenerates the plan from the decision and policy and compares it to the bound plan, requires the aggregation moment not to be later than the verification moment nor earlier than `generatedAt`, re-derives the duplicate/contradiction markings, the per-operation conclusions and the overall status purely from the bound receipt digests (which must follow their original order) and reason records, and finally checks the aggregator HMAC against the exact issuer/version key usable at the verification moment, so later revocation or expiry rejects it. On success it returns a fresh mapping keyed `aggregatedAt`, `confirmationDigest`, `decisionDigest`, `expiresAt`, `generatedAt`, `issuer`, `keyVersion`, `operations`, `planDigest`, `policyDigest`, `receipts`, `reasons`, `results`, `status` and `version`. Type faults raise `TypeError`; an illegal policy, keyring or moment raises `ValueError`; an illegal encoding, digest, order or binding raises `InvalidForkExecutionError` (a structurally bad receipt is only recorded as `invalid-receipt`, never raised); unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature raise `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_fork_confirmations(items, decision, policy, keyring, moment)` verifies a non-empty batch of those confirmations offline and in strict input order, in isolation. Each item contains exactly a non-empty, batch-unique `id` and `confirmation` bytes; the batch and shared decision, policy, keyring and moment are validated in full before any packet is verified, so only a batch-level fault raises (container/field faults `TypeError`; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id or a wrong item key set `ValueError`). Each packet is then reported as `verified`, `invalid` or `unauthenticated` with the fixed key order `error`, `id`, `result` and `status`; a failed item keeps a definite, non-empty copy of the original exception text and a null result, and the identity of an unauthenticated payload never enters a result. The top-level result has the fixed keys `items` and `version` (integer 1); repeated calls return equal but mutually independent results. The whole execution layer reads and writes no file and leaves every existing public interface and command unchanged.

## Multi-round fork convergence certificates

`certify_fork_convergence(rounds, decision, policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` certifies how one fork execution plan converged across several confirmation rounds, entirely offline, reading and writing no file and modifying no input. `rounds` is a non-empty list in chain order; each round carries exactly `seq` (the round number, consecutive from one), `previous` (the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the previous round's confirmation bytes, `null` for the first round) and the `confirmation` packet bytes. Every confirmation is re-checked through the exact `verify_fork_confirmation` rules at the certification moment and must bind the same plan, decision and policy; the aggregation moments must be strictly increasing across rounds, and a sequence gap, a broken chain link, a reordering or a duplicate is rejected. Each plan operation then converges in plan order: a `failed` round may advance to `executed` or `rejected` in a later round, but a settled execution or rejection must never be rolled back or swapped, and a re-execution binding a different post-state digest marks the operation `conflicted` — the settled evidence is kept, never overwritten by new evidence. One conflicted operation makes the overall status `conflicted`; otherwise an explicit rejection yields `rejected`, an unconverged operation `partial` and full convergence `confirmed`. Each result row carries exactly `operationId`, `target`, `result`, `settledRound` (null while unconverged) and `postDigest`, in plan order. The certificate is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte, carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds exactly `certifiedAt`, `decisionDigest`, `issuer`, `keyVersion`, `planDigest`, the per-round confirmation digests (`rounds`), the final `results`, the overall `status` and `version` (integer 1), and the signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the key bound to the exact issuer and version with no fallback. Parameter, container or field type faults raise `TypeError` (a `bool` never poses as an int); an empty round list, a wrong round key set, an empty confirmation or an illegal moment, issuer or version raises `ValueError`; a broken round chain or convergence relation raises `InvalidForkConvergenceError` (a `ValueError` subclass); a bad confirmation raises `InvalidForkExecutionError`; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials raise `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_fork_convergence(certificate, rounds, decision, policy, keyring, moment)` re-checks such a certificate entirely offline from just the certificate bytes, the original round chain and the shared materials — no file is read or written and no argument is modified. It validates the canonical encoding and key sets, re-walks the round chain (consecutive numbering, digest chaining, strictly increasing aggregation moments, one shared plan), re-verifies every bound confirmation at the certified moment, re-derives the per-operation convergence and overall status purely from the offered rounds, requires the bound round, plan and decision digests to match and the certification moment not to be later than the verification moment, and checks the HMAC against the key the current keyring binds to the payload's exact issuer and version, usable at the verification moment, so a later revocation or expiry rejects it. On success it returns a fresh mapping keyed `certifiedAt`, `certificateDigest`, `decisionDigest`, `issuer`, `keyVersion`, `planDigest`, `results`, `rounds`, `status` and `version` (integer 1). Type faults raise `TypeError`; an empty round list, a wrong round key set or an illegal policy, keyring or moment raises `ValueError`; a bad confirmation raises `InvalidForkExecutionError`; an illegal certificate encoding, key set, digest, round chain or convergence relation raises `InvalidForkConvergenceError`; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature raise `AuthenticationError`.

105	## Multi-site offline convergence adjudication
106	
107	`adjudicate_convergence(items, decision, policy, site_policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` turns single-site convergence certificates into one multi-site offline adjudication, reading and writing no file and modifying no input. `items` is a non-empty list; each item contains exactly a non-empty, batch-unique `id`, the `certificate` bytes and that certificate's non-empty `rounds` chain, and each item keeps the existing certificate identity and round-chain shape. `decision` is the original accepted fork decision bytes and `policy`/`keyring` are the shared fork materials used by the single-certificate rules. `site_policy` carries exactly `sites` (a non-empty mapping of each authorized non-empty signing site to its non-empty set of allowed positive key versions) and `threshold` (a positive integer no greater than the number of sites); `moment` is the current non-negative time and `issuer`/`version` name the adjudicator signing key. The whole batch — every round chain of every item, the shared materials and both policies — is validated in full before any certificate is reviewed: a nested type fault raises `TypeError` (a `bool` never poses as an int), while an empty round list or confirmation, a duplicate id or an illegal policy, threshold, moment, issuer or version raises `ValueError`.
108	
109	Each certificate is then independently re-checked through the exact single-certificate rules (its canonical shape, the decision and certification-moment bindings and a full re-convergence of its rounds), authorized by the exact signing site and key version against `site_policy` with no key fallback, and authenticated against the current keyring. An invalid certificate, unavailable/revoked/not-yet-valid/expired credential, unauthorized site or version or wrong signature rejects only that item with the fixed fork-adjudication reason (`invalid-proof`, `unauthorized-site`, `unauthorized-version`, `credential-unavailable`, `revoked`, `not-yet-valid`, `expired`, `bad-signature`) and the later items still run. For one site, certificates with the identical complete convergence result — the plan summary, the overall status and every operation's result, settled round and post-state digest — count once and every extra certificate is a `duplicate`; certificates with different complete results are a `contradiction`. Distinct sites must agree exactly on the plan summary, the overall status and every operation's result, settled round and post-state digest. Any self-contradiction or cross-site difference is `conflicted` with the common result set to null and cannot be outvoted by a majority; a unique complete result attested by at least the threshold of distinct sites is `accepted` and keeps the full convergence result; every other case is `insufficient`.
110	
111	The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object (recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved, no trailing byte) carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds exactly `certificates` (each certificate digest in the original input order), `common` (the complete shared convergence result, null unless accepted), `commonDigest` (the SHA-256 of the canonical common result, null unless accepted), `decisionDigest` (the SHA-256 of the original fork decision bytes), `issuer`, `keyVersion`, the per-certificate `items` (sorted stably by site then id, each carrying its `certificateDigest`, `convergence`, `conclusion`, `id`, `keyVersion`, `reason` and `site`), `planDigest` (the accepted plan digest, null otherwise), `policyDigest` (the SHA-256 of the canonical site policy), `status` and `version` (integer 1). The signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the key bound to the exact adjudicator issuer and version with no fallback; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired adjudicator credentials raise `AuthenticationError`.
112	
113	`verify_convergence_decision(decision_packet, decision, site_policy, keyring, moment)` re-checks such an adjudication entirely offline from just the packet, the original fork decision bytes, the expected site policy, the current keyring and the verification moment — no file is read or written and no argument is modified. It validates the canonical encoding and key sets, recomputes the fork decision and site policy digests, re-tallies the bound per-certificate items purely from the signed payload (the stable site/id ordering, the original-order certificate digest bindings, the same-site duplicate/contradiction markings, cross-site agreement, the threshold, the plan digest and the common result and digest), and checks the HMAC-SHA256 against the key the current keyring binds to the payload's exact issuer and version, usable at the verification moment, so a later revocation or expiry rejects it. On success it returns a fresh mapping keyed `certificates`, `common`, `commonDigest`, `convergenceDecisionDigest` (the SHA-256 of the packet), `decisionDigest` (the bound fork decision digest), `issuer`, `items`, `keyVersion`, `planDigest`, `policyDigest`, `status` and `version` (integer 1). A non-bytes argument or a wrong public field type raises `TypeError` (a `bool` never poses as an int); an empty value, a duplicate id or an illegal site policy, threshold, moment, site or version raises `ValueError`; an illegal packet structure or binding raises `InvalidConvergenceDecisionError` (a `ValueError` subclass); unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature raise `AuthenticationError`.
114	
115	`verify_convergence_decisions(items, decision, site_policy, keyring, moment)` verifies a non-empty batch of those adjudications offline and in strict input order, in isolation. Each item contains exactly a non-empty, batch-unique `id` and the `decision` packet bytes; the batch and the shared fork decision, site policy, keyring and moment are validated in full before any packet is verified, so only a batch-level fault raises (container/field faults `TypeError`; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id or a wrong item key set `ValueError`). Each packet is then reported in input order as `verified`, `invalid` or `unauthenticated` with the fixed key order `error`, `id`, `result` and `status`; a failed item keeps a definite, non-empty copy of the original exception text and a null result, and the identity of an unauthenticated payload never enters a result. The top-level result has the fixed keys `items` and `version` (integer 1); repeated calls return equal but mutually independent results. The existing convergence certificate, plan, confirmation and batch interfaces, and the module commands, are unchanged.
116	
117	
118	## Supersession chains over convergence decisions
119	
120	`supersede_decision(predecessor, evidence, decision, policy, old_policy, new_policy, keyring, moment, effective_at, issuer, version)` issues one signed successor packet that supersedes an existing convergence decision (the chain root) or the previous successor. `predecessor` is either packet; `evidence` is the stage's non-empty certificate/rounds list. The evidence sequence must have the predecessor as a strict prefix — a first successor keeps the root's certificates and ids in order, a later successor keeps every prior evidence item verbatim, so history is never deleted, changed or reordered; with an unchanged policy at least one new item is required, while a rotation may re-seal the same sequence. `decision`/`policy` are the original fork decision and shared fork policy, and `old_policy`/`new_policy` carry exactly `sites`, `threshold` and a positive integer `policyVersion`: unchanged sites and threshold keep the version, any change increments it by exactly one, and the root, plan and settled operations never change. The new verdict is recomputed from scratch from the full evidence: supplemental evidence moves `insufficient` to `accepted` or `conflicted`, an `accepted` verdict only keeps the identical common result or advances to `conflicted` (it never falls back to `insufficient` or swaps conclusions), and a `conflicted` verdict can never be masked by a later majority. The effective moment never moves backwards; the successor sealer and key version must be authorized by both policies and the credential must be usable both at `effective_at` and at the issuance `moment` (the same must hold for every evidence credential, or the settled verdict would differ at verify time). The packet is canonical compact UTF-8 JSON with exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds the root digest, predecessor digest, height, the full recomputed verdict (certificate digests in original order, items sorted by site then id, status, common result/digest and plan digest), the raw evidence increment (bytes carried as lowercase hex), the old/new policy digests, the policy version, the effective moment, the issuer and key version and `version` (integer 1), signed with HMAC-SHA256 under the exact issuer/version key. Parameter or field type faults raise `TypeError`; an empty value, duplicate id, illegal version or backwards moment raises `ValueError`; a malformed root raises `InvalidConvergenceDecisionError`; a malformed successor or any broken chain rule raises `InvalidChainError`; an identity the policies do not authorize raises `InvalidChainError`; a signature or credential fault raises `AuthenticationError`.
121	
122	`verify_decision_chain(root, successors, decision, policy, policies, keyring, moment)` verifies one chain hop by hop, entirely offline, reading and writing no file and modifying no input. `policies` provides one versioned site policy per stage (the root policy plus one per successor). The root is verified under the first policy's sites and threshold; every successor re-recomputes its verdict from the bound full evidence under its new policy at the hop's effective moment, re-checks the root, predecessor and height links, the old/new policy digests and version step, the non-decreasing effective moment and the append-only evidence prefix, re-applies the verdict state machine and dual-policy sealer authorization, requires the settled verdict to still hold with credentials usable at `moment`, and verifies the HMAC. It returns a fresh mapping with exactly `rootDigest`, `headDigest`, `height` (0 for a bare root), `policyVersion` and `status`; a bad root raises `InvalidConvergenceDecisionError`, a bad successor `InvalidChainError` and a signature or credential fault `AuthenticationError`.
123	
124	`verify_decision_chains(items, decision, policy, keyring, moment)` verifies a whole batch offline. Each item holds exactly a unique `id`, its `roots` packet, its ordered `successors` packets and its per-stage `policies`; the batch and shared materials are pre-validated in full, so only batch-level faults raise (container/field faults `TypeError`; an empty list, empty or duplicate id or wrong key set `ValueError`). Each chain is then reported in strict input order, in isolation, as `verified`, `invalid` or `unauthenticated` with the fixed key order `error`, `id`, `result` and `status`. One predecessor digest pointing at two distinct successor digests is a fork; a mere prefix extension (one chain growing longer along the same packets) is not. Every verified chain crossing a forking edge is reclassified `conflicted` with its verified result retained; chains that were invalid or unauthenticated are never reclassified. The result has the fixed keys `items` and `version` (integer 1).
125	
126	`seal_decision_head(items, target, decision, policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` seals a stable anchor only for the `target` chain within the batch that is `verified` (not conflicted by a fork), whose head is `accepted`. The anchor binds the target's root digest, head digest and height together with the head policy digest, head policy version and sealing moment and is signed under the exact issuer/version key; sealing a batch that is not entirely pre-validated, an unknown or empty target, a non-accepted/forked target or an illegal version raises `ValueError`, and a credential fault raises `AuthenticationError`. `verify_decision_head(anchor, items, target, decision, policy, keyring, moment)` re-checks the anchor structurally and its HMAC against the current key, re-runs the original batch and confirms the target still verifies, is accepted and unforked, and that every bound digest, height and version still matches; it returns `rootDigest`, `headDigest`, `height`, `policyDigest`, `policyVersion` and `anchorDigest`. A bad anchor raises `InvalidAnchorError` (a `ValueError` subclass); a batch fault raises the underlying `InvalidConvergenceDecisionError` or `InvalidChainError`; a signature or credential fault raises `AuthenticationError`. The adjudication, certificate, recovery command and `status` interfaces are unchanged and no new command-line entry is added.
127	
128	## Pruning multi-round convergence archives
129	
130	`plan_chain_prune(paths, checkpoint, decision, policy, keyring, moment)` builds a read-only signed plan for trimming persisted convergence archives, reading the archive files but never modifying, creating or deleting them. `paths` is an explicit, non-empty list of distinct file paths; each archive is one version-1 canonical JSON object (recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved, exactly one trailing `\n`) carrying exactly `project` (a unique non-empty identifier), `certificate` and the ordered `rounds` (each `{confirmation, seq}`, numbered consecutively from one), with the certificate and every confirmation carried as non-empty lowercase hex bytes. The sealing `checkpoint` is a `seal_chain_checkpoint` packet authenticated against the current keyring through the exact `verify_chain_suffix` rules (exact issuer/version, usable at `moment`, no fallback). An archive is eligible for pruning only when its certificate digest is part of the checkpoint's pruned evidence prefix and its whole round group re-verifies through the exact `verify_fork_convergence` rules against `decision`, `policy` and `keyring` at `moment`; non-eligible archives are retained and when nothing is eligible a `ValueError` is raised. The result is one canonical compact `{payload, signature}` object with no trailing byte; the payload binds exactly `checkpoint` (its SHA-256), `delete` (eligible projects ascending), `retain` (the SHA-256 of every retained archive's bytes, ascending), `source` and `target` (each a map from an eligible project to the digest of its archive bytes before pruning and of its trimmed project-marker archive afterwards) and `version` (integer 1). It carries no moment or project identifier of its own and is signed with the checkpoint's own exact issuer/key, so equal arguments produce byte-identical plans. Container/field type faults raise `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int); an empty/duplicate path or project, a wrong key set or an illegal version raises `ValueError`; a missing archive raises `FileNotFoundError`; an illegal archive or checkpoint raises `InvalidPruneError`; credential and signature faults raise `AuthenticationError`.
131	
132	`prune_chain_archives(items, keyring)` executes the plans in one controlled batch. Each item holds exactly a unique non-empty `id`, an archive `path`, the signed `plan`, the sealing `checkpoint` and a `header` naming the exact signing `issuer`/`keyVersion` (the checkpoint sealer) and the non-negative prune `moment`; the batch structure and keyring are validated first. Each item then runs in strict input order and full isolation: bad credentials, malformed plans or checkpoints and stale archives are recorded for that item alone, the archive is left unchanged and the batch continues. When the archive at `path` hashes to the plan's source digest for its project, the planned trimmed target (one canonical `{project, version}` marker ending in one `\n`, the certificate and all round bytes gone) is installed in a crash-safe two-phase transaction, and the receipt status is `pruned`; when the archive already hashes to the target digest nothing is written and the status is `duplicate`; any other content records `StalePruneError`. An `OSError` raised while writing, flushing, syncing a file or directory, replacing or deleting is recorded for that item with its original text and leaves the retryable transaction material in place. The transaction uses only same-directory files — a unique candidate, the hard-linked predecessor and the `path + ".prune.txn"` intent — whose only phases are `prepared` and `installed`; unrelated files are never scanned or touched. The batch returns, in input order, fresh dicts keyed `id`, `receipt` and `error`. The receipt is one canonical compact `{payload, signature}` object binding the `status`, the complete plan, the `checkpoint` digest, `beforeDigest`/`afterDigest` (equal for a duplicate), the full `delete` and `retain` digests, the prune `moment` and `version` 1, signed under the exact header key. The first completion and a same-plan re-entry (an interrupted transaction whose `.prune.txn` intent is still present) return one identical signed receipt: an installed same-plan intent is completed to the original `pruned` receipt and a prepared one is rolled back and retried.
133	
134	`recover_chain_prune(path)` settles one interrupted prune transaction, touching only the files its `path + ".prune.txn"` intent names. With no intent it returns `clean` without scanning artifacts, with the current archive digest (or `None` when the path is missing). A `prepared` intent rolls the source bytes back byte-for-byte from the retained predecessor (the path is removed again when it did not exist) and deletes the candidate, reporting `rolled-back`; an `installed` intent requires the current bytes to hash to `newDigest`, removes the remaining artifacts and reports `completed`; the intent is deleted last and the directory synced so a repeat returns `clean`, and every result carries the resulting digest. A non-str path raises `TypeError`; a malformed intent (wrong key set, version, phase, target, name confinement or digest binding, or a missing necessary artifact) raises `InvalidPruneError` without touching unrelated files; an `OSError` while reading, replacing, deleting or syncing propagates unchanged with the intent and artifacts retained for a retry. `InvalidPruneError` and `StalePruneError` both subclass `ValueError`. Planning and recovery read files but planning changes nothing; the existing checkpoint continuation verification, replacement chains, module commands and README command surface are unchanged.
135	
136	`verify_prune_receipt(receipt, checkpoint, keyring, moment)` verifies one signed prune receipt entirely offline — only the receipt bytes, the sealing checkpoint bytes, the current keyring and a non-negative moment are consulted, no file is read and no input is modified. The receipt must be a version-1 canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object (recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved, no trailing byte) carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds `afterDigest`, `beforeDigest`, `checkpoint`, `delete`, `moment`, the complete embedded `plan`, `retain`, `status` (`pruned` or `duplicate`) and `version`. The embedded plan must itself be the same canonical version-1 envelope, match the supplied checkpoint digest and signing identity/key version, and the receipt must repeat the plan's delete projects and retain digests exactly — a missing, extra, reordered or replaced entry is a broken binding. The checkpoint, plan and receipt signatures are all recomputed with the single key the checkpoint currently names (exact issuer/version, usable at `moment`) with no fallback. The unique plan target project is located solely from the status and before/after digests (zero or several candidates reject); the verifier then regenerates that project's version-1 prune marker itself, hashes its complete bytes, and requires the recomputed digest to match both the plan target and the receipt `afterDigest` — the receipt's derived conclusion is never trusted; a `pruned` receipt's `beforeDigest` must match the source archive and a `duplicate` receipt's both digests must match the target marker. It returns a fresh dict with the fixed key order `project`, `status`, `beforeDigest`, `afterDigest`, `checkpoint`, `planDigest`, `moment` and `version` (integer 1); repeated calls return equal, independent new objects. A wrong public argument type raises `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int) and an illegal moment raises `ValueError`; an illegal encoding, key set, version, digest, status or binding raises `InvalidPruneReceiptError` (a `ValueError` subclass, distinct from `InvalidPruneError`); unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or any signature error raise `AuthenticationError`.
137	
138	`verify_prune_receipts(items, keyring, moment)` verifies a batch of prune receipts offline. Each item holds exactly a batch-unique non-empty `id`, the `receipt` bytes and the sealing `checkpoint` bytes; the non-empty list, keyring and moment are pre-validated in full, so only batch-level faults raise (container/field faults `TypeError`, a bool rejected as an int; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, a wrong key set or an illegal moment `ValueError`). Each item is then verified in strict input order and in isolation through the exact `verify_prune_receipt` rules, reported as `verified`, `invalid` or `unauthenticated`; one item's failure never stops later items. The top-level result has exactly the fixed keys `items` and `version` (integer 1), and each report carries in fixed order `error` (`None` when verified, otherwise a definite non-empty message), `id`, `result` (a fresh single-entry result when verified, otherwise `None`) and `status`; repeated calls return equal but independent results.
139	## Signed prune attestations and multi-site threshold adjudication
140	
141	`sign_prune_attestation(items, batch, keyring, moment, site, version)` hands the conclusion of a prune receipt batch verification to an offline adjudicator. It takes the same non-empty `items` list as `verify_prune_receipts` (each item exactly a batch-unique non-empty `id`, the signed `receipt` bytes and the sealing `checkpoint` bytes), the authorized non-empty `batch` id, a `keyring`, the signing `moment` and the exact signing `site` and key `version`. The batch runs through the existing `verify_prune_receipts` verification in full, so only batch-level faults raise (container/element/public-field type faults `TypeError`, a bool never posing as an int; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, a wrong item key set, an empty batch or site or a non-positive/non-int version `ValueError`); one receipt's own failure is never raised. The `invalid` and `unauthenticated` items are kept exactly as the batch reported them — status, definite error text, a null `result` and all — and no trusted identity, project or boundary is ever filled in for them. The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte, carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`. The payload binds exactly `batch`, `items`, `keyVersion`, `moment`, `site` and `version` (integer 1); each item, in the original input order with no sorting, deduplication or replacement, carries exactly `checkpoint` (the lowercase hex SHA-256 of that item's checkpoint bytes), `id`, `receipt` (the SHA-256 of that item's receipt bytes) and `report` (that item's complete batch verification report, bound verbatim, with a verified report's result naming the same checkpoint digest). `signature` is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the key the keyring binds to the exact site and version with no fallback; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials raise `AuthenticationError`.
142	
143	`adjudicate_prune_attestations(items, policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` aggregates uniquely identified site attestations into one signed threshold decision, reading and writing no file and modifying no input. Each item holds exactly a unique non-empty `id` and `attestation` bytes. The `policy` carries exactly `batch` (the authorized batch id), `sites` (a non-empty map of each authorized non-empty site to its non-empty set of allowed positive key versions) and `threshold` (a positive integer no greater than the number of sites); `keyring` and `moment` keep their existing rules and `issuer`/`version` name the adjudicator credentials. Every attestation is re-checked by the exact signing site and key version named in its payload with no fallback: a structurally illegal packet is recorded `invalid-proof`, unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature `unauthenticated`, and a wrong batch, an unauthorized site or an unauthorized key version `unauthorized` — each rejecting only that item while the others continue. For one site, a packet counts only when the complete report and every receipt/checkpoint byte digest all agree; an exact repeat of the same content is `duplicate` and different valid content from one site is a `contradiction`. Distinct sites must agree on that same complete content: any cross-site report difference or bound-digest difference is a `conflicted` fork that a majority cannot outvote. A unique conflict-free content backed by at least the threshold of distinct sites is `accepted` and carries the one common complete report; the same one unique content short of the threshold stays `insufficient` but still carries that common report; a contradiction or disagreement is `conflicted`; and an `insufficient` tally with no valid vote at all binds a null report. The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte, carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds exactly `attestations` (each input attestation's SHA-256 in the original input order), `issuer`, `items` (the per-attestation rows sorted stably by site then id, each carrying `conclusion`, the attestation `digest`, the authenticated `entries` or null, `id`, `keyVersion`, `reason` and `site`), `keyVersion`, `policyDigest` (the SHA-256 of the canonical compact policy — sites ascending, each site's versions an ascending array), `report` (the common complete `{items, version}` batch report, or null), `status` and `version` (integer 1); the signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the exact adjudicator key. Parameter, container or public-field type faults raise `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int); an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, or an illegal batch, policy, threshold, moment, site or version raises `ValueError`; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired adjudicator credentials raise `AuthenticationError`.
144	
145	`verify_prune_adjudication(adjudication, policy, keyring, moment)` re-checks such a decision entirely offline from just the decision bytes, the expected `policy`, the current `keyring` and the verification moment, reading and writing no file and modifying no argument. It validates the canonical encoding and every key set, recomputes the policy digest, and re-tallies the bound per-attestation rows purely from the signed payload: the original-order attestation digest bindings, the site/id row ordering, same-site duplicate and contradiction markings, cross-site report and digest agreement, the threshold outcome and the claimed common report — any structure, digest, ordering or tally mismatch raises `InvalidPruneAdjudicationError`, which subclasses `ValueError`. It then checks the HMAC-SHA256 against the key the *current* keyring binds to the payload's exact issuer and version, usable at the verification moment, so a later revocation or expiry rejects the decision with no fallback; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature raise `AuthenticationError`. On success it returns a fresh dict equal to the authenticated payload (`attestations`, `issuer`, `items`, `keyVersion`, `policyDigest`, `report`, `status`, `version`); repeated calls return equal but mutually independent objects sharing no mutable structure. A non-bytes adjudication or a field of the wrong type raises `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int) and an illegal policy, keyring or moment raises `ValueError`.
146	
147	`verify_prune_adjudications(items, policy, keyring, moment)` verifies a non-empty batch of those decisions offline and in strict input order, in isolation. Each item holds exactly a unique non-empty `id` and the `adjudication` bytes; the whole batch structure, policy, keyring and moment are validated before any adjudication is parsed, so only batch-level faults raise (container/element/field type faults `TypeError`; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id or a wrong item key set `ValueError`, with policy, keyring and moment keeping their single-entry classification). One decision's failure never stops later items or changes an earlier report. Each item is reported in input order as `verified`, `invalid` (a structure or binding fault, including a tampered status or common report) or `unauthenticated` (unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature), with the fixed key order `error`, `id`, `result` and `status`; a failure keeps a definite, non-empty copy of the original exception text and a null result, and a verified item's result is a fresh deep copy of the authenticated adjudication payload. The top-level result has the fixed keys `items` and `version` (integer 1); repeated calls return equal but mutually independent results.
148	
149	`sign_prune_adjudication_batch(items, policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` packages one such batch verification into an offline handover packet. It takes the same non-empty `items` list as `verify_prune_adjudications` and runs that exact batch verification, so batch-level faults keep the same `TypeError`/`ValueError` classification (an empty issuer or a non-positive version additionally raises `ValueError`) while one decision's failure is never raised. The `invalid` and `unauthenticated` items are kept exactly as reported — status, definite error text and a null result — and no trusted issuer, project or prune boundary is filled in from unauthenticated content. The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte, carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds exactly `issuer`, `keyVersion`, `moment`, `policyDigest` (the SHA-256 of the canonical compact policy), `items` and `version` (integer 1). Each item, in the original input order with no sorting, deduplication or replacement, carries exactly `id`, `digest` (the lowercase hex SHA-256 of that item's original adjudication bytes) and `report` (that item's complete batch verification report, including the full authenticated adjudication payload when verified, bound verbatim). `signature` is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the exact issuer/version key; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials raise `AuthenticationError`.
150	
151	`verify_prune_adjudication_batch(packet, policy, keyring, moment)` re-checks a handover packet entirely offline from just the packet bytes, the expected `policy`, the current `keyring` and the verification moment, reading and writing no file and modifying no argument. It validates the canonical encoding and every key set, the original item order with each report's `id` positionally bound to its item, item-id uniqueness, every bound digest and the complete shape of every report — including a full structural validation and re-tally of each verified report's complete adjudication payload against the shared policy, recomputing the policy digest and rejecting a packet whose signing moment is later than the verification moment — before checking the HMAC-SHA256 against the exact current issuer/version key. A future moment, a duplicate id, a tampered report or a non-canonical encoding raises `InvalidPruneAdjudicationBatchError`, which subclasses `ValueError`; a non-bytes packet or a wrong field type raises `TypeError`; an illegal policy, keyring or moment raises `ValueError`; and unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature raise `AuthenticationError`. On success it returns a fresh deep copy of the authenticated payload (`issuer`, `keyVersion`, `moment`, `policyDigest`, `items`, `version`); repeated calls return equal but mutually independent objects. The existing chain pruning, recovery and receipt verification entry points and the README command surface are unchanged.
152	
153	## Cross-site aggregation of signed prune adjudication batches
154	
155	`aggregate_prune_batches(items, prune_policy, site_policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` converges the handover conclusions of several sites about one batch of prune adjudications into one signed cross-site aggregate, reading and writing no file and modifying no input. Each item contains exactly a unique non-empty `id` and `packet` bytes (a `sign_prune_adjudication_batch` handover packet); the whole batch structure — non-empty list, unique non-empty ids and bytes packets — must validate before any packet is parsed. `prune_policy` is the original `{"batch", "sites", "threshold"}` prune adjudication policy the handovers were issued against; `site_policy` carries exactly `sites` (a non-empty map of each authorized non-empty site to its non-empty set of allowed positive key versions) and `threshold` (a positive integer no greater than the number of sites); `keyring` keeps its existing validity/revocation rules and `moment` is the non-negative aggregation moment; `issuer`/`version` name the exact aggregate signing credentials.
156	
157	Each packet is first independently authenticated through the exact `verify_prune_adjudication_batch` rules — canonical structure, a signing moment no later than the aggregation moment, the exact original prune policy digest, a full re-tally of every verified embedded adjudication and an exact-issuer/version HMAC under a currently usable key — and then authorized precisely by the site and key version its payload names against the site policy, with no fallback. A structurally illegal packet, a future-dated handover, a packet bound to another prune policy or one with a broken embedded binding is recorded `invalid` with reason `invalid` (and carries no identity); unknown/revoked/not-yet-valid/expired credentials or a wrong HMAC are `unauthenticated`; an authenticated but unauthorized site or key version is `unauthorized` — one item's rejection never stops later items. A valid packet becomes that site's declaration: the complete authenticated handover item list in full original order, each entry binding its `id`, its input adjudication `digest` and its complete per-item verdict `report` (including every verified adjudication's full payload when verified), never compared by final status alone. For one site, an exactly field-identical declaration counts once and exact repeats are marked `duplicate`; any field-level difference between valid packets from one site is a `contradiction`. Different sites not sharing that exact complete declaration form a `conflicted` aggregate: the common declaration binds null and no majority can outvote the disagreement. A unique conflict-free declaration backed by at least the threshold of distinct sites is `accepted`; one unique declaration below threshold stays `insufficient` but keeps that common declaration; no valid vote at all binds a null declaration.
158	
159	Per-item conclusions are stably sorted by site then id, while the SHA-256 of every input packet is bound in original input order (`inputs`), so an input reordering is detectable. The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte, carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds exactly `inputs`, `issuer`, `items` (each row carrying `conclusion`, `digest`, `id`, `issuer`, `keyVersion`, `reason` and the authenticated `declaration` or null), `keyVersion`, `prunePolicyDigest` (the SHA-256 of the canonical original prune policy — sites ascending, versions ascending), `sitePolicyDigest` (the SHA-256 of the canonical site policy), `declaration` (the common complete original-order declaration, or null), `status` and `version` (integer 1). The signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the exact issuer/version key. A parameter, container or public-field type fault raises `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int); an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, or an illegal prune/site policy, threshold, moment, issuer or version raises `ValueError`; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired aggregate signing credentials raise `AuthenticationError`.
160	
161	`verify_prune_batch_aggregate(aggregate, prune_policy, site_policy, keyring, moment)` re-checks such an aggregate entirely offline from just the aggregate bytes, the two expected policies, the current keyring and the verification moment, reading and writing no file and modifying no argument. It validates the canonical encoding and every key set, recomputes both policy digests, and re-tallies the bound per-packet rows purely from the signed payload — original-order input digest bindings, issuer/id ordering, same-site duplicate/contradiction markings, cross-site declaration agreement (the complete original-order declarations, not just final statuses), threshold acceptance and the claimed common declaration — and structurally re-tallies every verified adjudication embedded in each bound declaration against the original prune policy, before checking the HMAC-SHA256 against the key the current keyring binds to the payload's exact issuer and version, usable at the verification moment, so a later revocation or expiry rejects with no fallback. A non-bytes aggregate or a public field of the wrong type raises `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int); an illegal prune/site policy, keyring or moment raises `ValueError`; an illegal aggregate encoding, key set, digest, ordering, tally or declaration binding raises `InvalidPruneBatchAggregateError`, which subclasses `ValueError`; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature raise `AuthenticationError`. On success it returns a fresh deep copy of the authenticated payload (`inputs`, `issuer`, `items`, `keyVersion`, `prunePolicyDigest`, `sitePolicyDigest`, `declaration`, `status`, `version`); repeated calls return equal but mutually independent objects sharing no mutable structure. The existing pruning, adjudication, batch verification and handover entry points and the README command surface are unchanged.
162	
163	## Supersession chains over cross-site prune batch aggregates
