## Multi-site offline convergence adjudication

`adjudicate_convergence(items, decision, policy, site_policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` turns single-site convergence certificates into one multi-site offline adjudication, reading and writing no file and modifying no input. `items` is a non-empty list; each item contains exactly a non-empty, batch-unique `id`, the `certificate` bytes and that certificate's non-empty `rounds` chain, and each item keeps the existing certificate identity and round-chain shape. `decision` is the original accepted fork decision bytes and `policy`/`keyring` are the shared fork materials used by the single-certificate rules. `site_policy` carries exactly `sites` (a non-empty mapping of each authorized non-empty signing site to its non-empty set of allowed positive key versions) and `threshold` (a positive integer no greater than the number of sites); `moment` is the current non-negative time and `issuer`/`version` name the adjudicator signing key. The whole batch — every round chain of every item, the shared materials and both policies — is validated in full before any certificate is reviewed: a nested type fault raises `TypeError` (a `bool` never poses as an int), while an empty round list or confirmation, a duplicate id or an illegal policy, threshold, moment, issuer or version raises `ValueError`.

Each certificate is then independently re-checked through the exact single-certificate rules (its canonical shape, the decision and certification-moment bindings and a full re-convergence of its rounds), authorized by the exact signing site and key version against `site_policy` with no key fallback, and authenticated against the current keyring. An invalid certificate, unavailable/revoked/not-yet-valid/expired credential, unauthorized site or version or wrong signature rejects only that item with the fixed fork-adjudication reason (`invalid-proof`, `unauthorized-site`, `unauthorized-version`, `credential-unavailable`, `revoked`, `not-yet-valid`, `expired`, `bad-signature`) and the later items still run. For one site, certificates with the identical complete convergence result — the plan summary, the overall status and every operation's result, settled round and post-state digest — count once and every extra certificate is a `duplicate`; certificates with different complete results are a `contradiction`. Distinct sites must agree exactly on the plan summary, the overall status and every operation's result, settled round and post-state digest. Any self-contradiction or cross-site difference is `conflicted` with the common result set to null and cannot be outvoted by a majority; a unique complete result attested by at least the threshold of distinct sites is `accepted` and keeps the full convergence result; every other case is `insufficient`.

The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object (recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved, no trailing byte) carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds exactly `certificates` (each certificate digest in the original input order), `common` (the complete shared convergence result, null unless accepted), `commonDigest` (the SHA-256 of the canonical common result, null unless accepted), `decisionDigest` (the SHA-256 of the original fork decision bytes), `issuer`, `keyVersion`, the per-certificate `items` (sorted stably by site then id, each carrying its `certificateDigest`, `convergence`, `conclusion`, `id`, `keyVersion`, `reason` and `site`), `planDigest` (the accepted plan digest, null otherwise), `policyDigest` (the SHA-256 of the canonical site policy), `status` and `version` (integer 1). The signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the key bound to the exact adjudicator issuer and version with no fallback; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired adjudicator credentials raise `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_convergence_decision(decision_packet, decision, site_policy, keyring, moment)` re-checks such an adjudication entirely offline from just the packet, the original fork decision bytes, the expected site policy, the current keyring and the verification moment — no file is read or written and no argument is modified. It validates the canonical encoding and key sets, recomputes the fork decision and site policy digests, re-tallies the bound per-certificate items purely from the signed payload (the stable site/id ordering, the original-order certificate digest bindings, the same-site duplicate/contradiction markings, cross-site agreement, the threshold, the plan digest and the common result and digest), and checks the HMAC-SHA256 against the key the current keyring binds to the payload's exact issuer and version, usable at the verification moment, so a later revocation or expiry rejects it. On success it returns a fresh mapping keyed `certificates`, `common`, `commonDigest`, `convergenceDecisionDigest` (the SHA-256 of the packet), `decisionDigest` (the bound fork decision digest), `issuer`, `items`, `keyVersion`, `planDigest`, `policyDigest`, `status` and `version` (integer 1). A non-bytes argument or a wrong public field type raises `TypeError` (a `bool` never poses as an int); an empty value, a duplicate id or an illegal site policy, threshold, moment, site or version raises `ValueError`; an illegal packet structure or binding raises `InvalidConvergenceDecisionError` (a `ValueError` subclass); unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature raise `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_convergence_decisions(items, decision, site_policy, keyring, moment)` verifies a non-empty batch of those adjudications offline and in strict input order, in isolation. Each item contains exactly a non-empty, batch-unique `id` and the `decision` packet bytes; the batch and the shared fork decision, site policy, keyring and moment are validated in full before any packet is verified, so only a batch-level fault raises (container/field faults `TypeError`; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id or a wrong item key set `ValueError`). Each packet is then reported in input order as `verified`, `invalid` or `unauthenticated` with the fixed key order `error`, `id`, `result` and `status`; a failed item keeps a definite, non-empty copy of the original exception text and a null result, and the identity of an unauthenticated payload never enters a result. The top-level result has the fixed keys `items` and `version` (integer 1); repeated calls return equal but mutually independent results. The existing convergence certificate, plan, confirmation and batch interfaces, and the module commands, are unchanged.


## Supersession chains over convergence decisions

`supersede_decision(predecessor, evidence, decision, policy, old_policy, new_policy, keyring, moment, effective_at, issuer, version)` issues one signed successor packet that supersedes an existing convergence decision (the chain root) or the previous successor. `predecessor` is either packet; `evidence` is the stage's non-empty certificate/rounds list. The evidence sequence must have the predecessor as a strict prefix — a first successor keeps the root's certificates and ids in order, a later successor keeps every prior evidence item verbatim, so history is never deleted, changed or reordered; with an unchanged policy at least one new item is required, while a rotation may re-seal the same sequence. `decision`/`policy` are the original fork decision and shared fork policy, and `old_policy`/`new_policy` carry exactly `sites`, `threshold` and a positive integer `policyVersion`: unchanged sites and threshold keep the version, any change increments it by exactly one, and the root, plan and settled operations never change. The new verdict is recomputed from scratch from the full evidence: supplemental evidence moves `insufficient` to `accepted` or `conflicted`, an `accepted` verdict only keeps the identical common result or advances to `conflicted` (it never falls back to `insufficient` or swaps conclusions), and a `conflicted` verdict can never be masked by a later majority. The effective moment never moves backwards; the successor sealer and key version must be authorized by both policies and the credential must be usable both at `effective_at` and at the issuance `moment` (the same must hold for every evidence credential, or the settled verdict would differ at verify time). The packet is canonical compact UTF-8 JSON with exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds the root digest, predecessor digest, height, the full recomputed verdict (certificate digests in original order, items sorted by site then id, status, common result/digest and plan digest), the raw evidence increment (bytes carried as lowercase hex), the old/new policy digests, the policy version, the effective moment, the issuer and key version and `version` (integer 1), signed with HMAC-SHA256 under the exact issuer/version key. Parameter or field type faults raise `TypeError`; an empty value, duplicate id, illegal version or backwards moment raises `ValueError`; a malformed root raises `InvalidConvergenceDecisionError`; a malformed successor or any broken chain rule raises `InvalidChainError`; an identity the policies do not authorize raises `InvalidChainError`; a signature or credential fault raises `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_decision_chain(root, successors, decision, policy, policies, keyring, moment)` verifies one chain hop by hop, entirely offline, reading and writing no file and modifying no input. `policies` provides one versioned site policy per stage (the root policy plus one per successor). The root is verified under the first policy's sites and threshold; every successor re-recomputes its verdict from the bound full evidence under its new policy at the hop's effective moment, re-checks the root, predecessor and height links, the old/new policy digests and version step, the non-decreasing effective moment and the append-only evidence prefix, re-applies the verdict state machine and dual-policy sealer authorization, requires the settled verdict to still hold with credentials usable at `moment`, and verifies the HMAC. It returns a fresh mapping with exactly `rootDigest`, `headDigest`, `height` (0 for a bare root), `policyVersion` and `status`; a bad root raises `InvalidConvergenceDecisionError`, a bad successor `InvalidChainError` and a signature or credential fault `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_decision_chains(items, decision, policy, keyring, moment)` verifies a whole batch offline. Each item holds exactly a unique `id`, its `roots` packet, its ordered `successors` packets and its per-stage `policies`; the batch and shared materials are pre-validated in full, so only batch-level faults raise (container/field faults `TypeError`; an empty list, empty or duplicate id or wrong key set `ValueError`). Each chain is then reported in strict input order, in isolation, as `verified`, `invalid` or `unauthenticated` with the fixed key order `error`, `id`, `result` and `status`. One predecessor digest pointing at two distinct successor digests is a fork; a mere prefix extension (one chain growing longer along the same packets) is not. Every verified chain crossing a forking edge is reclassified `conflicted` with its verified result retained; chains that were invalid or unauthenticated are never reclassified. The result has the fixed keys `items` and `version` (integer 1).

`seal_decision_head(items, target, decision, policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` seals a stable anchor only for the `target` chain within the batch that is `verified` (not conflicted by a fork), whose head is `accepted`. The anchor binds the target's root digest, head digest and height together with the head policy digest, head policy version and sealing moment and is signed under the exact issuer/version key; sealing a batch that is not entirely pre-validated, an unknown or empty target, a non-accepted/forked target or an illegal version raises `ValueError`, and a credential fault raises `AuthenticationError`. `verify_decision_head(anchor, items, target, decision, policy, keyring, moment)` re-checks the anchor structurally and its HMAC against the current key, re-runs the original batch and confirms the target still verifies, is accepted and unforked, and that every bound digest, height and version still matches; it returns `rootDigest`, `headDigest`, `height`, `policyDigest`, `policyVersion` and `anchorDigest`. A bad anchor raises `InvalidAnchorError` (a `ValueError` subclass); a batch fault raises the underlying `InvalidConvergenceDecisionError` or `InvalidChainError`; a signature or credential fault raises `AuthenticationError`. The adjudication, certificate, recovery command and `status` interfaces are unchanged and no new command-line entry is added.

## Pruning multi-round convergence archives

`plan_chain_prune(paths, checkpoint, decision, policy, keyring, moment)` builds a read-only signed plan for trimming persisted convergence archives, reading the archive files but never modifying, creating or deleting them. `paths` is an explicit, non-empty list of distinct file paths; each archive is one version-1 canonical JSON object (recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved, exactly one trailing `\n`) carrying exactly `project` (a unique non-empty identifier), `certificate` and the ordered `rounds` (each `{confirmation, seq}`, numbered consecutively from one), with the certificate and every confirmation carried as non-empty lowercase hex bytes. The sealing `checkpoint` is a `seal_chain_checkpoint` packet authenticated against the current keyring through the exact `verify_chain_suffix` rules (exact issuer/version, usable at `moment`, no fallback). An archive is eligible for pruning only when its certificate digest is part of the checkpoint's pruned evidence prefix and its whole round group re-verifies through the exact `verify_fork_convergence` rules against `decision`, `policy` and `keyring` at `moment`; non-eligible archives are retained and when nothing is eligible a `ValueError` is raised. The result is one canonical compact `{payload, signature}` object with no trailing byte; the payload binds exactly `checkpoint` (its SHA-256), `delete` (eligible projects ascending), `retain` (the SHA-256 of every retained archive's bytes, ascending), `source` and `target` (each a map from an eligible project to the digest of its archive bytes before pruning and of its trimmed project-marker archive afterwards) and `version` (integer 1). It carries no moment or project identifier of its own and is signed with the checkpoint's own exact issuer/key, so equal arguments produce byte-identical plans. Container/field type faults raise `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int); an empty/duplicate path or project, a wrong key set or an illegal version raises `ValueError`; a missing archive raises `FileNotFoundError`; an illegal archive or checkpoint raises `InvalidPruneError`; credential and signature faults raise `AuthenticationError`.

`prune_chain_archives(items, keyring)` executes the plans in one controlled batch. Each item holds exactly a unique non-empty `id`, an archive `path`, the signed `plan`, the sealing `checkpoint` and a `header` naming the exact signing `issuer`/`keyVersion` (the checkpoint sealer) and the non-negative prune `moment`; the batch structure and keyring are validated first. Each item then runs in strict input order and full isolation: bad credentials, malformed plans or checkpoints and stale archives are recorded for that item alone, the archive is left unchanged and the batch continues. When the archive at `path` hashes to the plan's source digest for its project, the planned trimmed target (one canonical `{project, version}` marker ending in one `\n`, the certificate and all round bytes gone) is installed in a crash-safe two-phase transaction, and the receipt status is `pruned`; when the archive already hashes to the target digest nothing is written and the status is `duplicate`; any other content records `StalePruneError`. An `OSError` raised while writing, flushing, syncing a file or directory, replacing or deleting is recorded for that item with its original text and leaves the retryable transaction material in place. The transaction uses only same-directory files — a unique candidate, the hard-linked predecessor and the `path + ".prune.txn"` intent — whose only phases are `prepared` and `installed`; unrelated files are never scanned or touched. The batch returns, in input order, fresh dicts keyed `id`, `receipt` and `error`. The receipt is one canonical compact `{payload, signature}` object binding the `status`, the complete plan, the `checkpoint` digest, `beforeDigest`/`afterDigest` (equal for a duplicate), the full `delete` and `retain` digests, the prune `moment` and `version` 1, signed under the exact header key. The first completion and a same-plan re-entry (an interrupted transaction whose `.prune.txn` intent is still present) return one identical signed receipt: an installed same-plan intent is completed to the original `pruned` receipt and a prepared one is rolled back and retried.

`recover_chain_prune(path)` settles one interrupted prune transaction, touching only the files its `path + ".prune.txn"` intent names. With no intent it returns `clean` without scanning artifacts, with the current archive digest (or `None` when the path is missing). A `prepared` intent rolls the source bytes back byte-for-byte from the retained predecessor (the path is removed again when it did not exist) and deletes the candidate, reporting `rolled-back`; an `installed` intent requires the current bytes to hash to `newDigest`, removes the remaining artifacts and reports `completed`; the intent is deleted last and the directory synced so a repeat returns `clean`, and every result carries the resulting digest. A non-str path raises `TypeError`; a malformed intent (wrong key set, version, phase, target, name confinement or digest binding, or a missing necessary artifact) raises `InvalidPruneError` without touching unrelated files; an `OSError` while reading, replacing, deleting or syncing propagates unchanged with the intent and artifacts retained for a retry. `InvalidPruneError` and `StalePruneError` both subclass `ValueError`. Planning and recovery read files but planning changes nothing; the existing checkpoint continuation verification, replacement chains, module commands and README command surface are unchanged.

`verify_prune_receipt(receipt, checkpoint, keyring, moment)` verifies one signed prune receipt entirely offline — only the receipt bytes, the sealing checkpoint bytes, the current keyring and a non-negative moment are consulted, no file is read and no input is modified. The receipt must be a version-1 canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object (recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved, no trailing byte) carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`; the payload binds `afterDigest`, `beforeDigest`, `checkpoint`, `delete`, `moment`, the complete embedded `plan`, `retain`, `status` (`pruned` or `duplicate`) and `version`. The embedded plan must itself be the same canonical version-1 envelope, match the supplied checkpoint digest and signing identity/key version, and the receipt must repeat the plan's delete projects and retain digests exactly — a missing, extra, reordered or replaced entry is a broken binding. The checkpoint, plan and receipt signatures are all recomputed with the single key the checkpoint currently names (exact issuer/version, usable at `moment`) with no fallback. The unique plan target project is located solely from the status and before/after digests (zero or several candidates reject); the verifier then regenerates that project's version-1 prune marker itself, hashes its complete bytes, and requires the recomputed digest to match both the plan target and the receipt `afterDigest` — the receipt's derived conclusion is never trusted; a `pruned` receipt's `beforeDigest` must match the source archive and a `duplicate` receipt's both digests must match the target marker. It returns a fresh dict with the fixed key order `project`, `status`, `beforeDigest`, `afterDigest`, `checkpoint`, `planDigest`, `moment` and `version` (integer 1); repeated calls return equal, independent new objects. A wrong public argument type raises `TypeError` (a bool never poses as an int) and an illegal moment raises `ValueError`; an illegal encoding, key set, version, digest, status or binding raises `InvalidPruneReceiptError` (a `ValueError` subclass, distinct from `InvalidPruneError`); unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or any signature error raise `AuthenticationError`.

`verify_prune_receipts(items, keyring, moment)` verifies a batch of prune receipts offline. Each item holds exactly a batch-unique non-empty `id`, the `receipt` bytes and the sealing `checkpoint` bytes; the non-empty list, keyring and moment are pre-validated in full, so only batch-level faults raise (container/field faults `TypeError`, a bool rejected as an int; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, a wrong key set or an illegal moment `ValueError`). Each item is then verified in strict input order and in isolation through the exact `verify_prune_receipt` rules, reported as `verified`, `invalid` or `unauthenticated`; one item's failure never stops later items. The top-level result has exactly the fixed keys `items` and `version` (integer 1), and each report carries in fixed order `error` (`None` when verified, otherwise a definite non-empty message), `id`, `result` (a fresh single-entry result when verified, otherwise `None`) and `status`; repeated calls return equal but independent results.
## Signed prune attestations and multi-site threshold adjudication

`sign_prune_attestation(items, batch, keyring, moment, site, version)` hands the conclusion of a prune receipt batch verification to an offline adjudicator. It takes the same non-empty `items` list as `verify_prune_receipts` (each item exactly a batch-unique non-empty `id`, the signed `receipt` bytes and the sealing `checkpoint` bytes), the authorized non-empty `batch` id, a `keyring`, the signing `moment` and the exact signing `site` and key `version`. The batch runs through the existing `verify_prune_receipts` verification in full, so only batch-level faults raise (container/element/public-field type faults `TypeError`, a bool never posing as an int; an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, a wrong item key set, an empty batch or site or a non-positive/non-int version `ValueError`); one receipt's own failure is never raised. The `invalid` and `unauthenticated` items are kept exactly as the batch reported them — status, definite error text, a null `result` and all — and no trusted identity, project or boundary is ever filled in for them. The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte, carrying exactly `payload` and `signature`. The payload binds exactly `batch`, `items`, `keyVersion`, `moment`, `site` and `version` (integer 1); each item, in the original input order with no sorting, deduplication or replacement, carries exactly `checkpoint` (the lowercase hex SHA-256 of that item's checkpoint bytes), `id`, `receipt` (the SHA-256 of that item's receipt bytes) and `report` (that item's complete batch verification report, bound verbatim, with a verified report's result naming the same checkpoint digest). `signature` is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the key the keyring binds to the exact site and version with no fallback; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials raise `AuthenticationError`.

`adjudicate_prune_attestations(items, policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version)` aggregates uniquely identified site attestations into one signed threshold decision, reading and writing no file and modifying no input. Each item holds exactly a unique non-empty `id` and `attestation` bytes. The `policy` carries exactly `batch` (the authorized batch id), `sites` (a non-empty map of each authorized non-empty site to its non-empty set of allowed positive key versions) and `threshold` (a positive integer no greater than the number of sites); `keyring` and `moment` keep their existing rules and `issuer`/`version` name the adjudicator credentials. Every attestation is re-checked by the exact signing site and key version named in its payload with no fallback: a structurally illegal packet is recorded `invalid-proof`, unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong signature `unauthenticated`, and a wrong batch, an unauthorized site or an unauthorized key version `unauthorized` — each rejecting only that item while the others continue. def verify_final_fork_decision_aggregate_chain_fork_decision(
    decision, prune_policy, authorization_policy, site_policy,
    signer_site_policy, adjudication_site_policy, proof_site_policy,
    keyring, moment,
):
    """Re-verify a signed final fork decision aggregate chain fork
    decision offline.

    Only the decision bytes, the expected shared ``prune_policy``, the
    invariant site ``authorization_policy``, the invariant fork-proof
    ``site_policy``, the invariant adjudication ``signer_site_policy``,
    the invariant issuing ``adjudication_site_policy``, the expected
    ``proof_site_policy``, the current ``keyring`` and the verification
    ``moment`` are consulted -- no file is read or written and no
    argument is modified.  The decision binds six policy digests (the
    prune policy, the site authorization policy, the fork-proof signer
    site policy, the adjudication signer site policy, the issuing
    adjudication site policy and the proof site policy).  Verification
    validates the canonical encoding and every key set, recomputes all
    six policy digests, re-tallies the bound per-proof rows purely from
    the signed payload (the term-by-term proof digest bindings over the
    canonical rows, the stable site/id row ordering, the same-site
    duplicate/contradiction markings, the cross-site declaration
    agreement, the signer threshold outcome and the claimed common
    declaration, which is an empty list when every authenticated proof
    attests a fork-free batch), and checks the HMAC-SHA256 against the
    key the current keyring binds to the payload's exact issuer and
    version, usable at the verification moment, so a later revocation
    or expiry rejects the decision with no fallback.

    On success a fresh depth-independent mapping is returned with the
    fixed keys ``common``, ``proofDigest`` (the SHA-256 of the decision
    bytes), ``issuer``, ``items``, ``keyVersion``,
    ``prunePolicyDigest``, ``proofs``, ``authorizationPolicyDigest``,
    ``sitePolicyDigest``, ``signerSitePolicyDigest``,
    ``adjudicationSitePolicyDigest``, ``proofSitePolicyDigest``,
    ``status`` and ``version`` (the integer 1); repeated calls return
    equal but mutually independent objects and unauthenticated
    identities and boundaries never enter a result.  A non-bytes
    decision or a wrong public field type raises :class:`TypeError` (a
    :class:`bool` never poses as an int); an empty value, a duplicate
    id, a wrong key set or an illegal policy, threshold, moment,
    identity or version raises :class:`ValueError`; an illegal decision
    structure, ordering, tally or binding raises
    :class:`InvalidFinalForkDecisionAggregateChainForkDecisionError` (a
    :class:`ValueError` subclass); unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or
    expired credentials or a wrong signature raise
    :class:`AuthenticationError`.
    """
    if not isinstance(decision, bytes):
        raise TypeError("decision must be bytes")
    materials = _ffdac_validated_materials(
        prune_policy, authorization_policy, site_policy,
        signer_site_policy, adjudication_site_policy,
    )
    validated_proof_site_policy = _validated_prune_batch_site_policy(
        proof_site_policy
    )
    _ffdacf_bind_proof_policy(materials, validated_proof_site_policy)
    _ffdac_bind_runtime(materials, keyring, moment)
    return _verify_ffdacf_decision_core(decision, materials)


def _verify_ffdacf_decision_core(decision: bytes, materials: dict):
    """Verify one final fork decision aggregate chain fork decision from
    materials.

    Shared core of
    :func:`verify_final_fork_decision_aggregate_chain_fork_decision`;
    the caller owns the argument-type and shared-material validation.
    The returned dict is freshly built solely from authenticated
    decision material.
    """
    payload, signature = _parse_ffdacf_decision(decision)
    _ffdacf_assert_digest_bindings(
        payload, materials, _FFDACF_DECISION_BINDING_CHECKS,
        _ffdacf_decision_invalid,
    )

    # The proof digest vector is bound term by term to the canonical
    # (stably sorted) rows, so a reordering of the summaries that is then
    # re-signed is rejected even though the digest multiset is unchanged.
    status = _reconcile_pafd(
        payload, materials["proof_site_policy"][ADJ_THRESHOLD],
        invalid=_ffdacf_decision_invalid, positional_proofs=True,
    )

    _ffdac_assert_payload_signature(
        materials["keyring"], payload[VD_ISSUER], payload[KEY_VERSION],
        materials["moment"], payload, signature,
        "final fork decision aggregate chain fork decision signature "
        "does not match",
    )

    return {
        PAFD_COMMON: copy.deepcopy(payload[PAFD_COMMON]),
        FORK_PROOF_DIGEST: hashlib.sha256(decision).hexdigest(),
        VD_ISSUER: payload[VD_ISSUER],
        ITEMS: copy.deepcopy(payload[ITEMS]),
        KEY_VERSION: payload[KEY_VERSION],
        PAFD_PRUNE_POLICY_DIGEST: materials["prune_policy_digest"],
        PAFD_PROOFS: list(payload[PAFD_PROOFS]),
        _ACF_AUTHORIZATION_POLICY_DIGEST:
            materials["authorization_policy_digest"],
        _ADCF_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST: materials["site_policy_digest"],
        _FACF_SIGNER_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST:
            materials["signer_site_policy_digest"],
        _FFDACF_ADJUDICATION_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST:
            materials["adjudication_site_policy_digest"],
        _FFDACF_PROOF_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST:
            materials["proof_site_policy_digest"],
        STATUS: status,
        VERSION: FINAL_FORK_DECISION_AGGREGATE_CHAIN_FORK_DECISION_VERSION,
    }

def aggregate_final_aggregate_chain_fork_decisions(
    items, prune_policy, authorization_policy, site_policy,
    signer_site_policy, adjudication_site_policy, decision_site_policy,
    keyring, moment, issuer, version,
):
    """Aggregate multi-site final aggregate chain fork decisions offline.

    ``items`` is a non-empty list; each item contains exactly a unique,
    non-empty str ``id`` and ``decision`` bytes produced by
    :func:`adjudicate_final_aggregate_chain_forks`; the whole batch
    structure is validated before any decision is parsed.
    ``prune_policy`` is the shared invariant original pruning policy,
    ``authorization_policy`` the invariant site authorization policy,
    ``site_policy`` the invariant fork-proof signer site policy,
    ``signer_site_policy`` the invariant adjudication signer site
    policy and ``adjudication_site_policy`` the invariant issuing site
    policy the decisions were issued against; ``decision_site_policy``
    carries exactly ``sites`` (a non-empty mapping of each decision
    site authorized to hand over decisions to its non-empty set of
    allowed positive key versions) and ``threshold`` (a positive
    integer no greater than the site count).  ``keyring`` follows the
    existing rules, ``moment`` is the current time and
    ``issuer``/``version`` name the aggregate signing identity and key
    version.  No file is read or written and no input is modified.

    Every decision is first re-verified on its own through the exact
    :func:`verify_final_aggregate_chain_fork_decision` rules --
    canonical structure, all five decision policy digest bindings, the
    term-by-term proof digest bindings and a full re-tally of the bound
    per-proof rows -- then authenticated against the current keyring by
    its exact payload issuer and key version, and finally authorized
    precisely against ``decision_site_policy`` with no fallback: a
    structurally illegal decision or one with a broken binding is
    recorded ``invalid`` with reason ``invalid`` (and carries no
    identity), unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials
    or a wrong signature ``unauthenticated``, and an authenticated but
    unauthorized site or key version ``unauthorized``, each rejecting
    only that item while the others continue.  A valid decision counts
    as the issuing site's complete declaration: the common fork edge
    set (empty for a fork-free decision), the per-item conclusions
    (stably sorted by site then id, each entry carrying its conclusion,
    proof digest, authenticated fork edges or null, id, reason and
    site), the term-by-term proof digest vector and the overall status.
    For one site, declarations fully identical on every field count
    once and exact repeats are ``duplicate``; any field difference is a
    ``contradiction``.  Distinct sites must agree on that same complete
    declaration -- any difference makes the aggregate ``conflicted``,
    the common declaration is bound null and no majority can outvote
    the disagreement.  One unique declaration backed by at least the
    threshold of distinct sites is ``accepted``; short of the threshold
    it stays ``insufficient`` but still carries that common
    declaration; with no valid vote the declaration is null.

    The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with
    recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte,
    carrying exactly ``payload`` and ``signature``.  The payload binds
    exactly ``inputs`` (each input decision's SHA-256 in the original
    input order), ``issuer``, ``items`` (the rows stably sorted by
    issuer then id, each carrying ``conclusion``, the decision
    ``digest``, ``id``, ``issuer``, ``keyVersion``, ``reason`` and the
    authenticated ``declaration`` or null), ``keyVersion``,
    ``prunePolicyDigest``, ``authorizationPolicyDigest``,
    ``sitePolicyDigest``, ``signerSitePolicyDigest``,
    ``adjudicationSitePolicyDigest``, ``decisionSitePolicyDigest``,
    ``declaration`` (the one common complete declaration, or null),
    ``status`` and ``version`` (the integer 1) -- six policy digests in
    total.  The signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the
    canonical compact payload bytes under the exact issuer/version key.

    A parameter, container or public field type fault raises
    :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an int); an
    empty list, an empty or duplicate id or an illegal policy,
    threshold, moment, site, version or issuer raises
    :class:`ValueError`; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired
    aggregate credentials raise :class:`AuthenticationError`.
    """
    validated_items = _validated_cfd_decision_items(items)
    validated_prune_policy = _validated_adjudication_policy(prune_policy)
    validated_authorization_policy = _validated_prune_batch_site_policy(
        authorization_policy
    )
    validated_site_policy = _validated_prune_batch_site_policy(site_policy)
    validated_signer_site_policy = _validated_prune_batch_site_policy(
        signer_site_policy
    )
    validated_adjudication_site_policy = _validated_prune_batch_site_policy(
        adjudication_site_policy
    )
    validated_decision_site_policy = _validated_prune_batch_site_policy(
        decision_site_policy
    )
    validated_keyring = _validated_keyring(keyring)
    aggregate_moment = _fe_moment(moment, "moment")
    if not isinstance(issuer, str):
        raise TypeError("issuer must be a str")
    if issuer == "":
        raise ValueError("issuer must be non-empty")
    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int):
        raise TypeError("version must be an int")
    if version <= 0:
        raise ValueError("version must be positive")

    prune_policy_digest = hashlib.sha256(
        _verdict_policy_bytes(validated_prune_policy)
    ).hexdigest()
    authorization_policy_digest = hashlib.sha256(
        _prune_batch_site_policy_bytes(validated_authorization_policy)
    ).hexdigest()
    site_policy_digest = hashlib.sha256(
        _prune_batch_site_policy_bytes(validated_site_policy)
    ).hexdigest()
    signer_site_policy_digest = hashlib.sha256(
        _prune_batch_site_policy_bytes(validated_signer_site_policy)
    ).hexdigest()
    adjudication_site_policy_digest = hashlib.sha256(
        _prune_batch_site_policy_bytes(validated_adjudication_site_policy)
    ).hexdigest()
    rows = [
        _aggregate_facfda_one(
            item,
            prune_policy_digest,
            authorization_policy_digest,
            site_policy_digest,
            signer_site_policy_digest,
            adjudication_site_policy_digest,
            validated_adjudication_site_policy[ADJ_THRESHOLD],
            validated_decision_site_policy,
            validated_keyring,
            aggregate_moment,
        )
        for item in validated_items
    ]
    input_digests = [row[CP_DIGEST] for row in rows]
    status, common_declaration = _tally_pfda_rows(
        rows, validated_decision_site_policy[ADJ_THRESHOLD]
    )
    rows.sort(
        key=lambda row: (
            row[VD_ISSUER] is not None,
            row[VD_ISSUER] or "",
            row[ID],
        )
    )

    signing_entry = _usable_checkpoint_key(
        validated_keyring, issuer, version, aggregate_moment
    )
    payload = {
        _FACFDA_INPUTS: input_digests,
        VD_ISSUER: issuer,
        ITEMS: rows,
        KEY_VERSION: version,
        _FACFDA_PRUNE_POLICY_DIGEST: prune_policy_digest,
        _FACFDA_AUTHORIZATION_POLICY_DIGEST: authorization_policy_digest,
        _FACFDA_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST: site_policy_digest,
        _FACFDA_SIGNER_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST: signer_site_policy_digest,
        _FACFDA_ADJUDICATION_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST:
            adjudication_site_policy_digest,
        _FACFDA_DECISION_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST: hashlib.sha256(
            _prune_batch_site_policy_bytes(validated_decision_site_policy)
        ).hexdigest(),
        _FACFDA_DECLARATION: common_declaration,
        STATUS: status,
        VERSION:
            FINAL_AGGREGATE_CHAIN_FORK_DECISION_AGGREGATE_VERSION,
    }
    signature = hmac.new(
        bytes.fromhex(signing_entry[SECRET]),
        _prune_compact(payload),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    return _prune_compact({TICKET_PAYLOAD: payload, SIGNATURE: signature})

def _reconcile_facfda_declaration(
    declaration: dict, fork_threshold: int, where: str
) -> None:
    """Re-tally one bound declaration as the decision it claims to be.

    The declaration's per-item conclusion entries and term-by-term proof
    digest vector are re-tallied through the exact final aggregate
    chain fork decision rules against the issuing site policy threshold,
    so a reordered entry, a reordered proof summary, a wrong duplicate
    or contradiction marking, a tampered common set or a mis-stated
    status cannot hide inside a counted declaration.  Any mismatch
    raises
    :class:`InvalidFinalAggregateChainForkDecisionAggregateError`.
    """
    synthetic_payload = {
        PAFD_COMMON: declaration[PAFD_COMMON],
        ITEMS: [
            {
                ADJ_CONCLUSION: entry[ADJ_CONCLUSION],
                PAFD_EDGES: entry[PAFD_EDGES],
                ID: entry[ID],
                KEY_VERSION: None,
                PAFD_FORK_PROOF_DIGEST: entry[CP_DIGEST],
                ADJ_REASON: entry[ADJ_REASON],
                VD_ISSUER: entry[VD_ISSUER],
            }
            for entry in declaration[PFDA_CONCLUSIONS]
        ],
        PAFD_PROOFS: declaration[PFDA_PROOFS],
        STATUS: declaration[STATUS],
    }
    try:
        _reconcile_pafd(
            synthetic_payload, fork_threshold,
            invalid=_facf_decision_invalid, positional_proofs=True,
        )
    except InvalidFinalAggregateChainForkDecisionError as exc:
        raise _facfda_invalid(f"{where}: {exc}") from exc


def _reconcile_facfda_aggregate(
    payload: dict, fork_threshold: int, decision_threshold: int
) -> None:
    """Re-derive every binding of a parsed decision aggregate payload.

    Re-tallies the per-decision rows the signature covers -- the
    original-order input digest bindings, row ordering, same-site
    duplicate and contradiction markings, cross-site complete
    declaration agreement, the threshold acceptance and the claimed
    common declaration and status -- and re-tallies every counted
    declaration against the issuing site policy threshold, without
    seeing any decision bytes.  Any mismatch raises
    :class:`InvalidFinalAggregateChainForkDecisionAggregateError`.
    """
    rows = payload[ITEMS]
    inputs = payload[_FACFDA_INPUTS]

    expected_order = sorted(
        rows,
        key=lambda row: (
            row[VD_ISSUER] is not None,
            row[VD_ISSUER] or "",
            row[ID],
        ),
    )
    if [row[ID] for row in expected_order] != [row[ID] for row in rows]:
        raise _facfda_invalid("items must be sorted by issuer then id")
    if sorted(row[CP_DIGEST] for row in rows) != sorted(inputs):
        raise _facfda_invalid(
            "the bound input digests must equal the per-item digests"
        )

    # Deep-copy the parsed rows before the tally mutates their
    # conclusion/reason markings; the signed payload itself is compared
    # through freshly derived structures only.
    working_rows = copy.deepcopy(rows)
    derived_status, derived_declaration = _tally_pfda_rows(
        working_rows, decision_threshold
    )

    for expected_row, bound_row in zip(working_rows, rows):
        if expected_row[ADJ_CONCLUSION] != bound_row[ADJ_CONCLUSION]:
            raise _facfda_invalid(
                f"item {bound_row[ID]!r} has the wrong conclusion"
            )
        if expected_row[ADJ_REASON] != bound_row[ADJ_REASON]:
            raise _facfda_invalid(
                f"item {bound_row[ID]!r} has the wrong reason"
            )

    if payload[STATUS] != derived_status:
        raise _facfda_invalid(
            "the bound status does not match the tallied items"
        )
    bound_declaration = payload[_FACFDA_DECLARATION]
    if derived_declaration is None:
        if bound_declaration is not None:
            raise _facfda_invalid(
                "the common declaration must be null when no unique "
                "conflict-free declaration was tallied"
            )
    else:
        if bound_declaration is None:
            raise _facfda_invalid(
                "an aggregate over one unique conflict-free declaration "
                "must carry the common declaration"
            )
        if bound_declaration != derived_declaration:
            raise _facfda_invalid(
                "the bound common declaration does not match the tallied "
                "decisions"
            )

    for row in rows:
        declaration = row[_FACFDA_DECLARATION]
        if declaration is None:
            continue
        _reconcile_facfda_declaration(
            declaration, fork_threshold, f"aggregate item {row[ID]!r}"
        )
    if bound_declaration is not None:
        _reconcile_facfda_declaration(
            bound_declaration, fork_threshold, "aggregate declaration"
        )

    key_version = payload[KEY_VERSION]
    if isinstance(key_version, bool) or not isinstance(key_version, int):
        raise TypeError("payload keyVersion must be an int")
    if key_version <= 0:
        raise _ffdacf_proof_invalid("payload keyVersion must be positive")
    moment = payload[CP_MOMENT]
    if isinstance(moment, bool) or not isinstance(moment, int):
        raise TypeError("payload moment must be an int")
    if moment < 0:
        raise _ffdacf_proof_invalid("payload moment must be non-negative")
    for field in (
        CF_PROOF_PRUNE_POLICY,
        _ACF_PROOF_AUTHORIZATION_POLICY,
        _ADCF_PROOF_SITE_POLICY,
        _FACF_PROOF_SIGNER_SITE_POLICY,
        _FFDACF_PROOF_ADJUDICATION_SITE_POLICY,
    ):
        digest = payload[field]
        if not isinstance(digest, str):
            raise TypeError(f"payload {field} must be a str")
        if not _prune_is_digest(digest):
            raise _ffdacf_proof_invalid(
                f"payload {field} must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
            )
    version = payload[VERSION]
    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int):
        raise TypeError("payload version must be an int")
    if version != FINAL_FORK_DECISION_AGGREGATE_CHAIN_FORK_PROOF_VERSION:
        raise _ffdacf_proof_invalid("payload version must be the integer 1")
    chains = _validated_pac_fork_chains(
        payload[FORK_PROOF_CHAINS], invalid=_ffdacf_proof_invalid
    )
    _validated_pac_fork_report(
        payload[FORK_PROOF_REPORT], chains,
        conflicted_error=_FFDAC_CHAIN_ITEM_ERROR,
        invalid=_ffdacf_proof_invalid,
        report_version=FINAL_FORK_DECISION_AGGREGATE_CHAINS_VERSION,
        require_fork=False,
        chain_result_validator=_validated_fac_fork_chain_result,
    )

# ===========================================================================
# Transferable fork proofs over final fork decision aggregate chain batches
# ===========================================================================
#
# This layer packages the
# :func:`verify_final_fork_decision_aggregate_chains` batch the way the
# final aggregate chain fork proof layer packages
# :func:`verify_final_aggregate_chains`, one stack higher: five
# *invariant* policies share the whole batch and are digested inside
# every signed proof -- the original prune policy, the site
# authorization policy, the fork-proof signer site policy, the
# adjudication signer site policy and the issuing adjudication site
# policy; the versioned decision site policy history is carried per
# stage inside the chain materials.  A proof may attest a fork-free
# batch: the fork edge collection is then bound empty and an
# authenticated proof still declares that empty set, and invalid or
# unauthenticated chains never contribute an edge.  Adjudication
# additionally takes the proof site policy that authorizes the exact
# proof signer identity and key version, and the decision binds six
# policy digests.

FINAL_FORK_DECISION_AGGREGATE_CHAIN_FORK_PROOF_VERSION = 1
FINAL_FORK_DECISION_AGGREGATE_CHAIN_FORK_DECISION_VERSION = 1

_FFDACF_PROOFS_VERSION = 1
_FFDACF_PROOFS_VERIFIED = _CF_PROOFS_VERIFIED
_FFDACF_PROOFS_INVALID = _CF_PROOFS_INVALID
_FFDACF_PROOFS_UNAUTHENTICATED = _CF_PROOFS_UNAUTHENTICATED

_FFDACF_PROOF_ADJUDICATION_SITE_POLICY = "adjudicationSitePolicy"
_FFDACF_ADJUDICATION_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST = "adjudicationSitePolicyDigest"
_FFDACF_PROOF_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST = "proofSitePolicyDigest"

_FFDACF_PROOF_PAYLOAD_KEYS = frozenset((
    FORK_PROOF_CHAINS,
    VD_ISSUER,
    KEY_VERSION,
    CP_MOMENT,
    CF_PROOF_PRUNE_POLICY,
    FORK_PROOF_REPORT,
    _ACF_PROOF_AUTHORIZATION_POLICY,
    _ADCF_PROOF_SITE_POLICY,
    _FACF_PROOF_SIGNER_SITE_POLICY,
    _FFDACF_PROOF_ADJUDICATION_SITE_POLICY,
    VERSION,
))

_FFDACF_DECISION_PAYLOAD_KEYS = frozenset((
    PAFD_COMMON,
    VD_ISSUER,
    ITEMS,
    KEY_VERSION,
    PAFD_PRUNE_POLICY_DIGEST,
    PAFD_PROOFS,
    _ACF_DECISION_AUTHORIZATION_POLICY_DIGEST,
    _ADCF_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST,
    _FACF_SIGNER_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST,
    _FFDACF_ADJUDICATION_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST,
    _FFDACF_PROOF_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST,
    STATUS,
    VERSION,
))

49057	    items, prune_policy, authorization_policy, site_policy,
49058	    signer_site_policy, adjudication_site_policy, keyring, moment,
49059	):
49060	    """Verify a whole batch of final fork decision aggregate chain fork
49061	    proofs offline.
49062	
49063	    ``items`` is a non-empty list; each item is a dict with exactly the
49064	    keys ``id`` (a non-empty str, unique across the batch) and ``proof``
49065	    (the bytes
49066	    :func:`sign_final_fork_decision_aggregate_chain_fork_proof`
49067	    produced).  The whole batch structure and the shared prune policy,
49068	    site authorization policy, fork-proof signer site policy,
49069	    adjudication signer site policy, issuing adjudication site policy,
49070	    keyring and moment are validated in full before any proof is
49071	    verified: container, element or field type faults raise
49072	    :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an int) and an
49073	    empty list, an empty or duplicate id or a wrong item key set raises
49074	    :class:`ValueError` (the shared materials keep their single-entry
49075	    classification).  Only these batch-level faults raise.
49076	
49077	    Each proof is then verified independently, in strict input order:
49078	    one proof's failure never stops a later proof or alters an earlier
49079	    report, and a failed item always keeps a null result and a definite
49080	    non-empty error.  Unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired
49081	    credentials or a wrong signature make the item
49082	    ``unauthenticated``; an illegal encoding, key set, version, digest,
49083	    count, ordering, reference or report binding makes it
49084	    ``invalid-proof``; a passing proof is ``verified`` and its result
49085	    carries ``proofDigest`` (the SHA-256 of the proof bytes).

49088	    and ``version`` (the integer 1); each item report carries, in this
49089	    key order, ``error`` (null exactly when verified), ``id``,
49090	    ``result`` (a fresh independent copy of the single-proof result
49091	    when verified, otherwise null -- the identity of an unauthenticated
49092	    payload never enters a result) and ``status``.  Repeated calls
49093	    return equal but mutually independent results.  No file is read or
49094	    written and no input is modified.
49095	    """

49099	        signer_site_policy, adjudication_site_policy,
49100	    )

49113	def _adjudicate_ffdacf_one(item: dict, materials: dict, moment: int) -> dict:
49114	    """Verify, authorize and authenticate one final fork decision
49115	    aggregate chain proof.
49116	
49117	    The proof is first checked through the exact final fork decision
49118	    aggregate chain fork proof structural rules, then the signing site
49119	    and key version are authorized exactly against the separate proof
49120	    site policy with no fallback, and finally the HMAC is checked
49121	    against the current keyring.  Any failure rejects just this row
49122	    with one fixed reason and never affects the other items.
49123	    """
49124	    item_id = item[ID]
49125	    raw_proof = item[FORK_PROOF_ITEM_PROOF]
49126	    proof_digest = hashlib.sha256(raw_proof).hexdigest()
49127

49130	            item_id, proof_digest, None, None, None,
49131	            _PAFD_CONCLUSION_INVALID, _PAFD_REASON_INVALID_PROOF,
49132	        )

49136	    except (TypeError, ValueError):

49141	    try:

49143	    except (TypeError, ValueError):

def _ffdacf_proofs_item_report(
    item_id: str, status: str, error: str | None, result: dict | None
) -> dict:
    """One final fork decision aggregate chain fork proof report, fixed
    key order."""
    return {
        CHECKPOINT_ITEM_ERROR: error,
        ID: item_id,
        VERDICT_ITEM_RESULT: result,
        STATUS: status,
    }


def _verify_ffdacf_fork_proof_item(item: dict, materials: dict) -> dict:
    """Verify one final fork decision aggregate chain fork proof in
    isolation.

    Unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials and a wrong
    signature make the item ``unauthenticated``; every encoding,
    key-set, version, digest, ordering, reference or report-binding
    fault makes it ``invalid-proof``; a passing proof is ``verified``.
    """
    item_id = item[ID]
    try:
        result = _verify_ffdacf_fork_proof_core(
            item[FORK_PROOF_ITEM_PROOF], materials
        )
    except AuthenticationError as exc:
        return _ffdacf_proofs_item_report(
            item_id, _FFDACF_PROOFS_UNAUTHENTICATED, str(exc), None
        )
    except (InvalidFinalForkDecisionAggregateChainForkProofError,
            TypeError) as exc:
        # A TypeError here can only come from a wrong JSON field type
        # *inside* the proof bytes; the public argument types were all
        # validated before the batch ran.
        return _ffdacf_proofs_item_report(
            item_id, _FFDACF_PROOFS_INVALID, str(exc), None
        )
    return _ffdacf_proofs_item_report(
        item_id, _FFDACF_PROOFS_VERIFIED, None, result
    )


def verify_final_fork_decision_aggregate_chain_fork_proofs(
    items, prune_policy, authorization_policy, site_policy,
    signer_site_policy, adjudication_site_policy, keyring, moment,
):
    """Verify a whole batch of final fork decision aggregate chain fork
    proofs offline.

    ``items`` is a non-empty list; each item is a dict with exactly the
    keys ``id`` (a non-empty str, unique across the batch) and ``proof``
    (the bytes
    :func:`sign_final_fork_decision_aggregate_chain_fork_proof`
    produced).  The whole batch structure and the shared prune policy,
    site authorization policy, fork-proof signer site policy,
    adjudication signer site policy, issuing adjudication site policy,
    keyring and moment are validated in full before any proof is
    verified: container, element or field type faults raise
    :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an int) and an
    empty list, an empty or duplicate id or a wrong item key set raises
    :class:`ValueError` (the shared materials keep their single-entry
    classification).  Only these batch-level faults raise.

    Each proof is then verified independently, in strict input order:
    one proof's failure never stops a later proof or alters an earlier
    report, and a failed item always keeps a null result and a definite
    non-empty error.  Unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired
    credentials or a wrong signature make the item
    ``unauthenticated``; an illegal encoding, key set, version, digest,
    count, ordering, reference or report binding makes it
    ``invalid-proof``; a passing proof is ``verified`` and its result
    carries ``proofDigest`` (the SHA-256 of the proof bytes).

    The top-level result is a fresh dict with the fixed keys ``items``
    and ``version`` (the integer 1); each item report carries, in this
    key order, ``error`` (null exactly when verified), ``id``,
    ``result`` (a fresh independent copy of the single-proof result
    when verified, otherwise null -- the identity of an unauthenticated
    payload never enters a result) and ``status``.  Repeated calls
    return equal but mutually independent results.  No file is read or
    written and no input is modified.
    """
    validated_items = _validated_pac_fork_proof_items(items)
    materials = _ffdac_validated_materials(
        prune_policy, authorization_policy, site_policy,
        signer_site_policy, adjudication_site_policy,
    )
    _ffdac_bind_runtime(materials, keyring, moment)
    return {
        ITEMS: [
            _verify_ffdacf_fork_proof_item(item, materials)
            for item in validated_items
        ],
        VERSION: _FFDACF_PROOFS_VERSION,
    }


# -- Multi-site threshold adjudication over the fork proofs -----------------

def _adjudicate_ffdacf_one(item: dict, materials: dict, moment: int) -> dict:
    """Verify, authorize and authenticate one final fork decision
    aggregate chain proof.

    The proof is first checked through the exact final fork decision
    aggregate chain fork proof structural rules, then the signing site
    and key version are authorized exactly against the separate proof
    site policy with no fallback, and finally the HMAC is checked
    against the current keyring.  Any failure rejects just this row
    with one fixed reason and never affects the other items.
    """
    item_id = item[ID]
    raw_proof = item[FORK_PROOF_ITEM_PROOF]
    proof_digest = hashlib.sha256(raw_proof).hexdigest()

    def structural_invalid() -> dict:
        return _cf_row(
            item_id, proof_digest, None, None, None,
            _PAFD_CONCLUSION_INVALID, _PAFD_REASON_INVALID_PROOF,
        )

    try:
        payload, signature, _chains = _parse_ffdacf_fork_proof(raw_proof)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return structural_invalid()

    site = payload[VD_ISSUER]
    key_version = payload[KEY_VERSION]
    try:
        edges = _pac_fork_proof_edges(payload)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return structural_invalid()

    def reject(reason: str) -> dict:
        return _cf_row(
            item_id, proof_digest, site, key_version, edges,
            _PAFD_CONCLUSION_INVALID, reason,
        )

    # All five shared policy digests must match and the proof must not
    # be dated after the adjudication moment; a mismatch makes the
    # claimed identity untrustworthy, so the row carries none.
    # Authorization itself is governed by the separate proof site
    # policy.
    if not _ffdacf_five_bindings_match(payload, materials):
        return structural_invalid()
    if payload[CP_MOMENT] > moment:
        return structural_invalid()

    proof_site_policy = materials["proof_site_policy"]
    keyring = materials["keyring"]
    allowed_versions = proof_site_policy[ADJ_SITES].get(site)
    if allowed_versions is None:
        return reject(REASON_UNAUTHORIZED_SITE)
    if key_version not in allowed_versions:
        return reject(REASON_UNAUTHORIZED_VERSION)

    key_entry = None
    for candidate in keyring.get(site, ()):
        if candidate[VERSION] == key_version:
            key_entry = candidate
            break
    if key_entry is None:
        return reject(REASON_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE)
    if key_entry[REVOKED]:
        return reject(REASON_REVOKED)
    if moment < key_entry[NOT_BEFORE]:
        return reject(REASON_NOT_YET_VALID)
    if moment > key_entry[NOT_AFTER]:
        return reject(REASON_EXPIRED)

    if not hmac.compare_digest(
        _ffdac_payload_signature(key_entry, payload), signature
    ):
        return reject(REASON_BAD_SIGNATURE)

    return _cf_row(
        item_id, proof_digest, site, key_version, edges,
        _PAFD_CONCLUSION_VALID, None,
    )

    contradicted, votes = _tally_pac_fork_rows(rows)

    if contradicted or len(declarations) > 1:
        status = _CF_STATUS_CONFLICTED
        common = None
    elif len(declarations) == 1:
        common = _sorted_pac_fork_edge_objects(next(iter(declarations)))
        if len(votes) >= validated_proof_site_policy[ADJ_THRESHOLD]:
            status = _CF_STATUS_ACCEPTED
        else:
            status = _CF_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT
    else:
        status = _CF_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT
        common = None

    rows.sort(
        key=lambda row: (
            row[VD_ISSUER] is not None,
            row[VD_ISSUER] or "",
            row[ID],
        )
    )
    # The proof summary vector corresponds term by term to the canonical
    # (sorted) rows, so a reordering of the summaries that is then
    # re-signed is detectable offline without seeing any proof even
    # though the digest multiset is unchanged.
    proof_digests = [row[_CF_PROOF_DIGEST] for row in rows]

    signing_entry = _usable_checkpoint_key(
        materials["keyring"], issuer, version, moment
    )
    payload = {
        _CF_DECISION_COMMON: common,
        VD_ISSUER: issuer,
        ITEMS: [copy.deepcopy(row) for row in rows],
        KEY_VERSION: version,
        PAFD_PRUNE_POLICY_DIGEST: materials["prune_policy_digest"],
        _CF_DECISION_PROOFS: proof_digests,
        _ACF_DECISION_AUTHORIZATION_POLICY_DIGEST:
            materials["authorization_policy_digest"],
        _ADCF_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST: materials["site_policy_digest"],

def _parse_ffdacf_decision(raw: object) -> tuple[dict, str]:
    """Validate final fork decision aggregate chain fork decision bytes
    structurally.

    A non-bytes argument or a field of the wrong type raises
    :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an int); every
    encoding, key-set, version, digest or value-format fault raises
    :class:`InvalidFinalForkDecisionAggregateChainForkDecisionError`.
    The six policy bindings, the tally and the signature are checked by
    the decision verifier.
    """
    data, payload, signature = _ffdac_parse_envelope(
        raw, noun="decision", invalid=_ffdacf_decision_invalid,
        reject_duplicate=_reject_duplicate_ffdacf_decision_keys,
        payload_keys=_FFDACF_DECISION_PAYLOAD_KEYS,
        payload_keys_error=(
            "payload must contain exactly the keys 'common', 'issuer', "
            "'items', 'keyVersion', 'prunePolicyDigest', 'proofs', "
            "'authorizationPolicyDigest', 'sitePolicyDigest', "
            "'signerSitePolicyDigest', 'adjudicationSitePolicyDigest', "
            "'proofSitePolicyDigest', 'status' and 'version'"
        ),
        top_keys=_PAFD_DECISION_TOP_KEYS,
    )

    issuer = payload[VD_ISSUER]
    if not isinstance(issuer, str):
        raise TypeError("payload issuer must be a str")
    if issuer == "":
        raise _ffdacf_decision_invalid(
            "payload issuer must be a non-empty str"
        )
    key_version = payload[KEY_VERSION]
    if isinstance(key_version, bool) or not isinstance(key_version, int):
        raise TypeError("payload keyVersion must be an int")
    if key_version <= 0:
        raise _ffdacf_decision_invalid("payload keyVersion must be positive")
    status = payload[STATUS]
    if not isinstance(status, str):
        raise TypeError("payload status must be a str")
    if status not in _PAFD_STATUSES:
        raise _ffdacf_decision_invalid(
            "payload status is not a known status"
        )
    for field in (
        PAFD_PRUNE_POLICY_DIGEST,
        _ACF_DECISION_AUTHORIZATION_POLICY_DIGEST,
        _ADCF_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST,
        _FACF_SIGNER_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST,
        _FFDACF_ADJUDICATION_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST,
        _FFDACF_PROOF_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST,
    ):
        digest = payload[field]
        if not isinstance(digest, str):
            raise TypeError(f"payload {field} must be a str")
        if not _prune_is_digest(digest):
            raise _ffdacf_decision_invalid(
                f"payload {field} must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
            )

    proofs = payload[PAFD_PROOFS]
    if not isinstance(proofs, list):
        raise TypeError("payload proofs must be a list")
    if not proofs:
        raise _ffdacf_decision_invalid("payload proofs must be non-empty")
    for position, digest in enumerate(proofs):
        if not isinstance(digest, str):
            raise TypeError(f"payload proof {position} digest must be a str")
        if not _prune_is_digest(digest):
            raise _ffdacf_decision_invalid(
                f"payload proof {position} digest must be 64 lowercase hex "
                "characters"
            )

    raw_rows = payload[ITEMS]
    if not isinstance(raw_rows, list):
        raise TypeError("payload items must be a list")
    if not raw_rows:
        raise _ffdacf_decision_invalid("payload items must be non-empty")
    seen_ids: set[str] = set()
    for position, row in enumerate(raw_rows):
        where = f"payload item {position}"
        if not isinstance(row, dict):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} must be an object")
        if set(row.keys()) != _PAFD_ROW_KEYS:
            raise _ffdacf_decision_invalid(
                f"{where} must contain exactly the keys 'conclusion', "
                "'edges', 'id', 'keyVersion', 'digest', 'reason' and "
                "'site'"
            )

27593	    """Validate aggregate bytes structurally into ``(payload, signature)``.

27600	    digests, tally and credential bindings are checked by
27601	    :func:`verify_prune_fork_decision_aggregate`.

27603	    if not isinstance(raw, bytes):
27604	        raise TypeError("aggregate packet must be bytes")

27608	            "trailing byte"
27609	        )

"""Tests for batch verification and cross-site aggregation of final
aggregate chain fork decisions.

Covers :func:`verify_final_aggregate_chain_fork_decisions`,
:func:`aggregate_final_aggregate_chain_fork_decisions` and
:func:`verify_final_aggregate_chain_fork_decision_aggregate`: the
decision batch container and six shared materials validated in full
before any decision is parsed, the per-decision
verified/invalid-decision/unauthenticated taxonomy with input-order
reports and no cross-decision interference, the
verify-then-authenticate-then-authorize per-decision aggregation
pipeline with its fixed invalid/unauthenticated/unauthorized reasons,
same-site duplicate/contradiction handling over the complete
declaration (the common fork edge set, empty for a fork-free decision,
the per-item conclusions sorted by site then id, the term-by-term proof
digest vector and the overall status), cross-site declaration
agreement with no majority override, threshold acceptance with the
common declaration kept on insufficient tallies, the canonical signed
aggregate packet and its six policy digest bindings, the offline
re-tally verification recomputing every binding plus each counted
declaration, the aggregate credential rules, the distinct error
hierarchy, equal-but-independent results, input immutability and the
purely offline guarantee.
"""

import copy
import hashlib
import hmac
import json
import os
import sys
import unittest
from unittest import mock

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

from offline_coordination.replication import (
    AuthenticationError,
    InvalidFinalAggregateChainForkDecisionAggregateError,
    InvalidFinalAggregateChainForkDecisionError,
    SECRET,
    adjudicate_final_aggregate_chain_forks,
    aggregate_final_aggregate_chain_fork_decisions,
    sign_final_aggregate_chain_fork_proof,
    verify_final_aggregate_chain_fork_decision,
    verify_final_aggregate_chain_fork_decisions,
    verify_final_aggregate_chain_fork_decision_aggregate,
    _prune_batch_site_policy_bytes,
    _prune_compact,
    _usable_checkpoint_key,
    _validated_keyring,
    _verdict_policy_bytes,
)

from test_supersede_final_aggregate import FinalAggregateChainFixtures
from test_aggregate_prune_fork_decisions import decision_item
from test_prune_attestations import JUDGE, SITE_A, SITE_B, SITE_C

JUDGE_B = SITE_C
BATCH_REPORT_KEYS = ["items", "version"]
ITEM_REPORT_KEYS = ["error", "id", "result", "status"]
AGGREGATE_KEYS = ["payload", "signature"]
AGGREGATE_PAYLOAD_KEYS = [
    "adjudicationSitePolicyDigest", "authorizationPolicyDigest",
    "decisionSitePolicyDigest", "declaration", "inputs", "issuer",
    "items", "keyVersion", "prunePolicyDigest", "signerSitePolicyDigest",
    "sitePolicyDigest", "status", "version",
]
AGGREGATE_ROW_KEYS = [
    "conclusion", "declaration", "digest", "id", "issuer", "keyVersion",
    "reason",
]
DECLARATION_KEYS = ["common", "conclusions", "proofs", "status"]
AGGREGATE_RESULT_KEYS = [
    "aggregateDigest", "inputs", "issuer", "items", "keyVersion",
    "prunePolicyDigest", "authorizationPolicyDigest", "sitePolicyDigest",
    "signerSitePolicyDigest", "adjudicationSitePolicyDigest",
    "decisionSitePolicyDigest", "declaration", "status", "version",
]
SINGLE_RESULT_KEYS = [
    "common", "proofDigest", "issuer", "items", "keyVersion",
    "prunePolicyDigest", "proofs", "authorizationPolicyDigest",
    "sitePolicyDigest", "signerSitePolicyDigest",
    "adjudicationSitePolicyDigest", "status", "version",
]


def compact(obj):
    """One canonical compact envelope, matching the production encoding."""
    return _prune_compact(obj)


def parse(raw):
    return json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))


class FinalFinalFixtures(FinalAggregateChainFixtures):
    """Signed final-layer decisions from two decision sites."""

    def setUp(self):  # noqa: D102
        super().setUp()
        # The invariant fork-proof signer site policy digested inside
        # each final proof (distinct from the adjudication signer site
        # policy of the lower aggregate-decision layer).
        self.fsignerp = {
            "sites": {SITE_A: {1}, SITE_B: {1}}, "threshold": 2}
        # The invariant issuing/adjudication site policy authorizing the
        # exact proof signer identity and key version inside a decision.
        self.adjp = {
            "sites": {SITE_A: {1}, SITE_B: {1}, SITE_C: {1}},
            "threshold": 2}
        # The decision site policy authorizes the decision sites.
        self.dsp = {"sites": {JUDGE: {1}, JUDGE_B: {1}}, "threshold": 2}
        self.ffork_proofs = [
            {"id": "x", "proof": self.facf_proof(self.fork_items, SITE_A)},
            {"id": "y", "proof": self.facf_proof(self.fork_items, SITE_B)},
        ]
        self.ffree_proofs = [
            {"id": "x",
             "proof": self.facf_proof(self.clean_items, SITE_A)},
            {"id": "y",
             "proof": self.facf_proof(self.clean_items, SITE_B)},
        ]
        self.decision_ja = self.facf_decision(self.ffork_proofs, JUDGE)
        self.decision_jb = self.facf_decision(self.ffork_proofs, JUDGE_B)
        self.free_ja = self.facf_decision(self.ffree_proofs, JUDGE)
        self.free_jb = self.facf_decision(self.ffree_proofs, JUDGE_B)

    def facf_proof(self, items, issuer=SITE_A, moment=None):
        return sign_final_aggregate_chain_fork_proof(
            items, self.policy, self.auth, self.ssp, self.fsignerp,
            self.ring, self.m if moment is None else moment, issuer, 1)

    def facf_decision(self, proofs, issuer=JUDGE, moment=None, ring=None):
        return adjudicate_final_aggregate_chain_forks(
            proofs, self.policy, self.auth, self.ssp, self.fsignerp,
            self.adjp, self.ring if ring is None else ring,
            self.m if moment is None else moment, issuer, 1)

    def fdecision_items(self):
        return [
            decision_item("one", self.decision_ja),
            decision_item("two", self.decision_jb),
        ]

    def fbatch_report(self, items, ring=None, moment=None):
        return verify_final_aggregate_chain_fork_decisions(
            items, self.policy, self.auth, self.ssp, self.fsignerp,
            self.adjp, self.ring if ring is None else ring,
            self.m if moment is None else moment)

    def fmake_aggregate(self, items, dsp=None, ring=None, moment=None,
                       issuer=JUDGE, version=1):
        return aggregate_final_aggregate_chain_fork_decisions(
            items, self.policy, self.auth, self.ssp, self.fsignerp,
            self.adjp, self.dsp if dsp is None else dsp,
            self.ring if ring is None else ring,
            self.m if moment is None else moment, issuer, version)

    def fverify_aggregate(self, raw, dsp=None, ring=None, moment=None):
        return verify_final_aggregate_chain_fork_decision_aggregate(
            raw, self.policy, self.auth, self.ssp, self.fsignerp,
            self.adjp, self.dsp if dsp is None else dsp,
            self.ring if ring is None else ring,
            self.m if moment is None else moment)

    def rewrap(self, payload, moment=None, issuer=None, version=None):
        """Re-seal an edited payload (default JUDGE aggregate key)."""
        sign_issuer = payload.get("issuer") if issuer is None else issuer
        sign_version = (
            payload.get("keyVersion") if version is None else version)
        at = self.m if moment is None else moment
        entry = _usable_checkpoint_key(
            _validated_keyring(self.ring), sign_issuer, sign_version, at)
        payload_bytes = _prune_compact(payload)
        signature = hmac.new(
            bytes.fromhex(entry[SECRET]), payload_bytes,
            hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
        return _prune_compact(
            {"payload": payload, "signature": signature})

    def assert_invalid(self, raw, dsp=None, ring=None, moment=None):
        with self.assertRaises(
            InvalidFinalAggregateChainForkDecisionAggregateError
        ):
            self.fverify_aggregate(raw, dsp=dsp, ring=ring, moment=moment)


class BatchValidationTest(FinalFinalFixtures, unittest.TestCase):
    def test_non_list_items_is_type_error(self):
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.fbatch_report((decision_item("one", self.decision_ja),))

    def test_empty_list_is_value_error(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.fbatch_report([])

    def test_non_dict_item_is_type_error(self):
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.fbatch_report(["nope"])

    def test_wrong_item_key_set(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.fbatch_report([{"id": "one", "decision":
                                self.decision_ja, "extra": 1}])

    def test_non_str_id(self):

            self.fbatch_report([{"id": 1, "decision": self.decision_ja}])

    def test_empty_id(self):

    def test_duplicate_id(self):

                decision_item("one", self.decision_ja),

    def test_bool_moment_never_poses_as_int(self):

                self.fdecision_items(), self.policy, self.auth, self.ssp,

class BatchReportTest(FinalFinalFixtures, unittest.TestCase):
    def test_two_verified_decisions(self):
        report = self.fbatch_report(self.fdecision_items())
        self.assertEqual(list(report.keys()), BATCH_REPORT_KEYS)
        self.assertEqual(report["version"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(len(report["items"]), 2)
        for item in report["items"]:
            self.assertEqual(list(item.keys()), ITEM_REPORT_KEYS)
            self.assertEqual(item["status"], "verified")
            self.assertIsNone(item["error"])
            self.assertIsInstance(item["result"], dict)
            self.assertEqual(set(item["result"]), set(SINGLE_RESULT_KEYS))

    def test_input_order_preserved(self):
        report = self.fbatch_report(list(reversed(self.fdecision_items())))
        self.assertEqual([i["id"] for i in report["items"]], ["two", "one"])

    def test_invalid_decision_does_not_block_later(self):
        report = self.fbatch_report([
            decision_item("bad", b"not a packet"),
            decision_item("ok", self.decision_jb)])
